• Full compliance with BP 344 providing barrier-free access through elevators, ramps, handrails, and PWD-friendly restrooms.
• Gender-inclusive toilets and safe, well-lit circulation areas that promote comfort, safety, and inclusivity for all users.
• Clearly marked emergency exits, fire detection and suppression systems, alarms, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes.
5. Alignment with CDRRM and Sustainability Frameworks
• Integration into the campus’ Comprehensive Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (CDRRM) Plan.
• Building readiness to serve as temporary evacuation or emergency response facility during disasters.
• Consistency with EVSU’s Infrastructure Sustainability Adaptation Framework and Green Campus Roadmap.

With a total gross floor area of 3,291.75 sq.m., the facility is designed to be fully comply with all PWD regulatory and statutory requirements, and be equipped with sustainable, energy-efficient, and climate-resilient systems. column4: Construction of Five-Storey EVSU Ormoc (Luna) Academic Building
column6:
The project is part of the priority development list of FY2025 under the Eastern Visayas State University (EVSU) Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP). The Construction of the Five-Storey Academic Building for EVSU Ormoc (Luna) Campus is envisioned as a modern, climate-resilient, and inclusive facility that responds to the increasing academic and operational demands of the campus. With steady growth in enrollment—particularly in engineering and technology programs—the current physical infrastructure can no longer adequately support instructional delivery, specialized training, and student services.

The proposed academic building will optimize the limited campus land area through vertical development, providing additional learning spaces and improving functional efficiency. The ground and second floors will each house three (3) specialized laboratories and a faculty office, while the third to fifth floors will provide five (5) classrooms per level, complemented by student lounges and support spaces. Each floor will include gender-inclusive comfort rooms, and dedicated utility/electrical service rooms, ensuring effective building operations.

The proposed project have an approximate gross floor area of 3291.75 sq.m. which will have PWD-compliant services and accessibility features. The Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) is P198,342,367.00 for its completion integrating DRR/CCA measures, sustainable materials, and energy-efficient systems to ensure long-term resilience, cost efficiency, and institutional sustainability.

The project is essential not only for addressing spatial deficiencies but also for advancing EVSU’s commitment to building safe, resilient, and future-ready learning environments. As part of the university’s sustainability direction, the building integrates principles of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) in compliance with national standards and in alignment with SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

According to the hazard and risk assessment under the LUDIP, the project site is not prone to flooding, storm surge, tsunami, or liquefaction, but is situated in an area with high susceptibility to landslide and a moderate ground shaking hazard (PEIS VII). Thus, structural and site development measures will be prioritized to ensure long-term safety, durability, and operational continuity of the facility.

DRR/CCA Features
1. Hazard-Responsive Structural Design
•	Seismic design features aligned with updated national earthquake-resilient building standards, considering Leyte’s active tectonic environment.
•	High-wind-resistant structural framing, roof anchorage, and building envelope to withstand strong typhoons common in Ormoc City.
•	Reinforced and elevated foundation system to minimize the effects of soil instability and ensure building stability over time.
2. Climate-Adaptive Infrastructure
•	Installation of a rainwater harvesting system to augment non-potable water requirements and reduce demand on the main water supply.
•	Improved stormwater management through drainage upgrades, retention mechanisms, and permeable pavement to avoid localized flooding.
•	Solar-ready roofing system designed for future integration of photovoltaic panels to reduce dependency on grid electricity.
•	Building orientation and design optimized for natural lighting and ventilation, reducing energy consumption and improving indoor comfort.
3. Sustainability and Green Campus Integration
•	Use of energy-efficient and climate-appropriate building materials such as insulated wall panels, reflective roofing, and low-emissivity glazing.
•	Adoption of low-VOC, eco-friendly construction materials to promote healthier indoor environments.
•	Landscaping interventions, including native tree planting, to support biodiversity, enhance shade, improve microclimate, and contribute to long-term carbon reduction goals.
4. Inclusivity, Accessibility, and Safety
•	Full compliance with BP 344 accessibility standards, including ramps, handrails, elevator access, and PWD-friendly restrooms.
•	Gender-responsive spaces and inclusive comfort room provisions to accommodate a diverse student population.
•	Installation of fire detection, alarm, and suppression systems, along with well-defined evacuation routes and emergency signage.
5. Operational Continuity and DRRM Integration
•	Direct integration of the building into the overall Campus DRRM Plan, ensuring its use as a functional evacuation point or temporary command post during emergencies.
•	Provision for backup power supply supporting essential campus functions such as ICT equipment, emergency lighting, and communication systems.
•	Design of select classrooms and laboratories to operate as temporary safe holding areas during disasters.

column4: Redesigning the University Library Spaces into a State of the Art Learning Commons Model.
column6:
A library is a crucial aspect of a student's educational experience; it is sometimes referred as the heart of the university, but it must be updated to keep up with technology advancements and changing expectations of 21st-century students. The concept of a library has evolved much beyond its physical structure. The notion of the learning commons is a new service model implemented by several university libraries in the country and abroad, to suit students' educational and research needs. In support of education, collaboration, and student growth in the digital age, the learning commons model merges traditional library services with the new world of information in a seamless physical and virtual environment.
	The Learning Commons concept at the University Library and Information Services is intended to provide a collaborative service to enhance student learning and foster a research culture at our institution. The university library, as a support to Academic Services, must foster a culture of change based on user demands. Rapid developments in technology, information access, and how students study and use information necessitate a rethinking of all we do in the library, including how we address students' complex learning demands.

column4: Construction of Small Water Impounding Facility (Flood Mitigation Project for Sustainable Development)
column6: The Small Water Impounding Project (SWIP) at Central Luzon State University (CLSU) is an innovative and sustainable initiative aimed at addressing frequent flooding in the university during rainy season and the growing water scarcity issues in the region during dry season, particularly for agricultural use. The project is designed to capture and store rainwater or excess surface water during the wet season, providing a reliable water source during the dry months for irrigation, livestock, and other agricultural activities. By establishing a SWIP at CLSU, the university aims to engage to the community to improve people’s lives through skills training and other livelihood programs in relation to agri-aqua production and climate change adaptation and mitigation, and boost the University’s agritourism through showcasing R&D generated technologies for agriculture. The small water impounding system is a earth fill structure to be built across a narrow depression within CLSU compound to harvest and store rainfall and runoff for immediate and multiple use such as irrigation, fish pond and recreational park.

Of this number, 1.3 million were beneficiaries from 112 state universities and colleges while at least 300,000 were from local SUCs.

column4: Construction of the Two-Storey EVSU Tanauan Campus Research Development and Extension Services Resource and Training Center
column6:
As part of the priority projects listed in FY2025 under the university's Land Used Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP), the construction of the Tw0-Storey EVSU Tanauan Campus Research, Development, and Extension Services (RDE) Resource and Training Center, with a total project cost of P56,097,500.00, is proposed to enhance the university's capacity for research excellence, innovation, and community-focused extension services while strengthening institutional resilience and climate adaptability.

Situated in a region frequently exposed to typhoons, strong winds, and seismic activity, the facility is designed with comprehensive Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Change Adaptation (DRR/CCA) measures to ensure long-term stability, safety, and uninterrupted operations. The project integrates climate-resilient construction materials, reinforced structural systems, elevated floor levels, and advanced stormwater management solutions capable of withstanding earthquakes, extreme weather events, and other climate-induced hazards.

Based on the EVSU LUDIP Hazard and Risk Assessment, the project site has low susceptibility to flooding, no exposure to storm surge, high susceptibility to tsunami and liquefaction, no landslide risk, and moderate seismic exposure (PEIS VII). Accordingly, the building design incorporates robust DRR/CCA interventions to mitigate these risks and safeguard both infrastructure and occupants.

The RDE Center will be constructed on a newly donated lot from the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Tanauan, reflecting strong intergovernmental cooperation in advancing inclusive, innovation-driven, and climate-resilient development for the region. This initiative supports EVSU’s mandate to build academic infrastructure that not only responds to instructional and research needs but also enhances community preparedness, knowledge transfer, and adaptive capacity.

The facility will accommodate offices for Research, Development, Innovation, and Extension Services, as well as a fully equipped Training Center capable of hosting workshops, seminars, technology transfer activities, and capacity-building programs for students, faculty, LGUs, partner agencies, and local communities. The design ensures universal accessibility, gender sensitivity, and inclusivity, featuring ramps, elevators, barrier-free circulation routes, and gender-inclusive restrooms compliant with BP 344 and GAD standards.

Aligned with the EVSU LUDIP, the Infrastructure Sustainability Adaptation (ISA) Framework, and national sustainable development agendas, the project contributes to the university’s goals of climate-resilient, innovative, and inclusive campus development. It also supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals—particularly SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

Integrated DRR/CCA Features
1. Structural Resilience
•	Earthquake-resistant design compliant with NSCP 2015.
•	Reinforced concrete framing and foundations capable of withstanding high-wind events such as typhoons and tornado-level gusts.
•	Use of corrosion-resistant, climate-adaptive materials suitable for high-moisture and salt-air environments.
2. Flood and Tsunami Adaptation
•	Elevated ground floor to minimize exposure to potential floodwaters.
•	Perimeter grading, swales, and climate-adaptive landscaping to facilitate stormwater flow and soil stabilization.
•	Integration of sustainable drainage and stormwater retention systems.
•	Emergency signage and evacuation planning aligned with tsunami hazard maps.
3. Passive Cooling and Energy Efficiency
•	Optimized natural ventilation and daylighting to reduce heat stress and energy consumption.
•	Installation of insulated roofing, LED lighting, and reflective exterior materials.
•	Provision for future solar photovoltaic (PV) system integration.
•	Rainwater harvesting systems for non-potable uses (irrigation, flushing, and cleaning).
4. Emergency Preparedness and DRRM Integration
•	Safe egress routes, emergency exits, and designated evacuation areas.
•	Fire detection, alarm, and suppression systems in compliance with the Fire Code of the Philippines.
•	Emergency power capacity for critical functions during disasters.
•	Dedicated DRR training rooms to support community and campus disaster preparedness initiatives.
5. Environmental Sustainability
•	Use of green, locally sourced, and low-VOC materials.
•	Installation of water-saving and energy-efficient fixtures.
•	Landscaping using native, drought-tolerant, and climate-resilient species to improve microclimate and reduce heat island effect.

At present, many of these students incur high transportation costs and experience extended travel times that adversely affect their attendance, study hours, and overall academic performance. By providing on-campus housing, the project aims to improve accessibility to educational facilities, minimize logistical barriers to learning, and support student retention and completion rates.

The dormitory will be designed with integrated support services to ensure a functional and student-centered facility. A mini-grocery and reasonably priced dining options will be operated by the Community Business Operations (CBO) unit, reinforcing the university’s approach to providing both convenience and affordability. The inclusion of all-inclusive rental packages covering utilities such as water, electricity, and optional internet services will further reduce the administrative and financial burden on students, enabling them to focus on their studies. These provisions are consistent with institutional efforts to create conducive learning environments and to promote gender-responsive facilities.

column4: Construction of  Two-Storey EVSU Tanauan Campus Student and Health & Wellness Facility
column6:
As part of the priority projects for FY 2025 of the approved Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP) of the university, the proposed Construction of the Two-Storey EVSU Tanauan Campus Student Center, and Health & Wellness Facility, with an estimated cost of Sixty-One Million Six Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 61,960,675), is a strategic development initiative designed to enhance student welfare, leadership, engagement, and holistic learning. As the central hub for student services, the facility will consolidate essential programs and create an environment conducive to academic support, psychosocial well-being, and vibrant student life. This project ensures alignment with the university’s commitment to sustainable, resilient, and inclusive campus development. It further supports EVSU’s broader vision to be the National University for Resilience and Climate Action, contributing to national priorities for disaster-ready schools and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) — particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

In response to the increasing demand for student support services and the growing campus population, this facility will integrate modern spaces for the Student Affairs and Services Office (SASO), the Office of the Student Government (OSG), multi-purpose activity venues, and a campus Health and Wellness Unit. It will provide safe, inclusive, efficient, and future-ready environments that strengthen the academic and extracurricular ecosystem of EVSU Tanauan.

As indicated in the EVSU LUDIP Hazard and Risk Assessment, the project site has low susceptibility for flooding, not susceptible to storm surge, high susceptibility to tsunami and liquefaction, not susceptible to landslide, and categorized as having moderate seismic exposure (PEIS VII) for ground shaking. The design therefore incorporates robust Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) interventions to ensure long-term structural integrity and operational continuity.

Integrated DRR/CCA Features
The facility is designed to be disaster-resilient, climate-adaptive, and environmentally sustainable, ensuring the continuity of essential student services, even during extreme events. Key DRR/CCA measures include:

1. Hazard-Responsive Structural Design
•	Engineered to comply with the latest National Building Code of the Philippines and relevant DPWH structural guidelines.
•	Reinforced structural framework designed to withstand moderate to strong seismic events, recognizing Tanauan’s proximity to active fault systems.
•	Typhoon-resilient roofing and façade systems capable of resisting high wind speeds common to Region VIII.
•	Use of durable, long-lasting, and climate-resilient construction materials to reduce lifecycle costs and ensure long-term structural integrity.
2. Climate-Adaptive and Environmentally Responsive Features
•	Optimized natural ventilation and daylighting to reduce heat buildup and energy consumption.
•	Installation of solar-ready roofing infrastructure, enabling future integration of renewable energy systems.
•	Rainwater harvesting systems for non-potable water use (sanitation, landscape irrigation).
•	Climate-smart architectural features such as sunshades, heat-reflective exterior materials, and cross-ventilation corridors to reduce indoor heat stress.
•	Stormwater management systems including improved drainage and surface runoff controls to manage intense rainfall events.
3. DRRM-Focused Site Planning and Safety Systems
•	Integration into the campus-wide Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) Plan.
•	Design provision for:
o	Emergency exits and evacuation routes
o	Fire detection and suppression systems
o	Emergency lighting and signages
o	Safe refuge areas within or adjacent to the structure
•	The facility may serve as a temporary coordination or shelter area during campus emergencies.
4. Sustainability and Green Campus Integration
•	Use of eco-friendly, low-VOC materials to promote indoor air quality.
•	Landscaping with native vegetation for natural cooling, soil stabilization, and improved microclimate.
•	Water- and energy-efficient fixtures to minimize resource consumption.
•	Waste management systems supporting the university’s goal of a greener, cleaner campus.
5. Inclusivity, Safety, and Accessibility
•	Fully PWD-compliant with ramps, elevators, tactile indicators, and accessible restrooms following BP 344 (Accessibility Law).
•	Gender-sensitive facilities, including separate restrooms for men, women, all-gender users, and persons with diverse needs.
•	Safe, well-lit corridors and public spaces promoting comfort, safety, and security for all students.

The Two-Storey Student Center and Health Wellness Facility will serve as a cornerstone of student life at EVSU Tanauan Campus. Beyond providing essential student services and wellness support, the facility represents the university’s forward-looking commitment to resilient, sustainable, and inclusive infrastructure development. By integrating DRR/CCA principles, the project ensures operational continuity, enhances campus preparedness, and provides a safer, more supportive environment for all students.

A reliable residential infrastructure allows faculty and staff to focus on teaching, research, and community service responsibilities without concerns over housing security, thereby optimizing their contribution to institutional objectives, operational efficiency, and service delivery.

column4: CONSTRUCTION OF TWO-STOREY EXECUTIVE BUILDING AT PANGANIBAN CAMPUS
column6:
The existing Panganiban Campus Executive Building, constructed more than three decades ago, has significantly deteriorated over time due to exposure to multiple super typhoons affecting the Province of Catanduanes, compounded by structural damage from termite infestation. The facility, built with outdated design standards and materials, no longer meets the safety, durability, and functionality requirements for institutional use.

At present, the Executive Building serves as a critical support facility for billeting external evaluators, accreditors, visiting professors, and other institutional partners who conduct academic and administrative engagements at the Panganiban Campus. However, its current state poses both safety risks and operational limitations. Given the absence of commercial lodging establishments within the municipality and the lack of reliable 24-hour transport services connecting Panganiban (located 58 kilometers from Virac), the demand for on-campus accommodation remains essential.

The proposed project involves the expansion and redevelopment of the existing structure into a modern two-storey reinforced concrete building, designed to comply with current structural codes and resilient construction standards. The project scope includes the fabrication, acquisition, and installation of appropriate furnishings and fixtures to make the facility fully occupancy-ready upon completion. By addressing both safety and serviceability concerns, the project contributes to the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) sector outcomes on expanding access to quality education services and strengthening resilient infrastructure. It also supports regional development by enhancing institutional readiness for accreditation, fostering academic collaborations, and enabling sustainable socio-economic growth in geographically isolated areas such as Northern Catanduanes.

column4: Completion  of 5 Storey Academic Building, Baungon Campus
column6:
Currently, the project has completed the construction of its three floors following Phase 1 and Phase 2 construction. The existing structure is already functional and serves as a learning space for students, featuring classrooms and stairways that are accessible and operational. However, the building still shows unfinished portions such as exposed beams and columns that indicate provisions for additional floors. While the structure is stable, it lacks final architectural finishes like façade treatment, plastering, and painting that would enhance both its appearance and durability. To fully realize the intended design, the project requires the construction of the remaining two floors to complete the academic building. The completion of these additional levels will accommodate six more classrooms, each having 72 square meters of floor area that could accommodate 45-50 male and female students, and improve the overall capacity of the campus to serve its growing student population. An estimated amount of ₱35,000,000.00 is needed to complete the construction and finishing works, which include structural, electrical, and architectural components essential for the building’s full functionality and safety compliance.

For safety and disaster resilience, the building adheres to the provisions set by the Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Change Adaptation (DRRCCA) standards. It is equipped with emergency exits, fire alarms, sprinklers, and clearly marked evacuation plan signage, ensuring the safety of students, faculty, and staff in case of emergencies. These features are essential for preventing fire-related incidents, facilitating quick evacuation, and minimizing potential hazards during unforeseen events such as earthquakes or other natural disasters. By incorporating these measures, the building is designed to prioritize the well-being of its occupants while complying with safety regulations. To promote inclusivity and accessibility, the building includes facilities that cater to persons with disabilities (PWDs), gender and development (GAD) initiatives, and senior citizens. Specially designed restrooms for PWDs are installed to accommodate their needs, ensuring ease of use and convenience. Additionally, ramps with protective
barricades are integrated into the design to provide safe and comfortable access for individuals using wheelchairs or those with mobility challenges. These features are crucial in fostering an inclusive learning environment, ensuring that all individuals, regardless of their physical abilities, can navigate the building with ease. Beyond its functional aspects, the academic building also reflects the university’s dedication to cultural sensitivity. The architectural design incorporates elements inspired by the indigenous culture of Bukidnon, blending traditional and modern influences. The building’s facade features intricate patterns, symbols, and colors that pay homage to the province’s rich cultural heritage. This integration of local artistic elements not only enhances the aesthetic appeal of the building but also fosters a sense of identity and pride among students, faculty, and the surrounding community. By embedding cultural significance into its design, the building serves as a representation of the university’s respect for and commitment to preserving local traditions. Similar to the university’s existing infrastructure, the new academic building will uphold DRRCCA provisions, ensuring compliance with safety and disaster preparedness standards. It will also incorporate accessibility features for PWDs, GAD, and senior citizens, reinforcing the institution’s commitment to inclusivity. Furthermore, the building will be constructed using green architectural principles, emphasizing sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental responsibility. 

As part of its long-term development plan, the construction of the academic building is included as an attributed Program, Activity, and Project (PAP) under the 2026 BukSU Gender and Development (GAD) planning and budget. This inclusion reflects the university’s strategic approach to infrastructure development, ensuring that gendersensitive, inclusive, and sustainable designs are prioritized. To guarantee the successful execution of this project, BukSU will continue its capacity-building initiatives for project implementers and the monitoring team. These initiatives will equip personnel with the necessary skills and expertise to oversee project planning, implementation, and evaluation, ensuring quality and adherence to institutional goals.

column4: Completion of 5-Storey Academic Building-Phase 2, Kalilangan Campus
column6:
The project is currently in its initial phase of structural development, with several reinforced concrete columns already erected and aligned according to the site plan. These columns, complete with vertical reinforcement bars, establish a solid foundation and indicate readiness for the next phase of construction. In light of this, it is imperative that the project be continued to ensure the timely completion of the planned academic building in BukSU Kalilangan. The existing foundation provides a strong basis for vertical expansion, minimizing the need for additional groundwork. Furthermore, resuming the construction at this stage will prevent further weathering of exposed materials, optimize the resources already utilized, and uphold the project’s intended purpose and design integrity. To continue its construction, an additional amount of ₱50,000,000.00 is needed for the 5-storey Academic Building at BukSU Kalilangan Campus. This funding will cover the completion of the ground floor structural works, ensuring that the space becomes functional and ready for academic use. The proposed continuation of construction aims to address the urgent need for additional learning facilities to accommodate the growing male and female student populations on campus.

The completion of Phase 2 will result in the establishment of three (3) academic classrooms, each having 72 square meters of floor area that could accommodate 45-50 male and female students, along with a toilet facility and storage area on the ground floor. To continue its construction, an additional amount of ₱50,000,000.00 is needed for the 5-storey Academic Building at BukSU Kalilangan Campus. This funding will cover the completion of the ground floor structural works, ensuring that the space becomes functional and ready for academic use. The proposed continuation of construction aims to address the urgent need for additional learning facilities to accommodate the growing male and female student populations on campus. The completion of Phase 2 will result in the establishment of three (3) academic classrooms, each having 72 square meters of floor area that could accommodate 45-50 male and female students, along with a toilet facility and storage area on the ground floor. The conception of the project has involved careful planning and participation of the various stakeholders of the university. The participation of both men and women in
various beneficiary groups in problem identification and project design was crucial in the planning process of the project. In addition, the conduct of gender analysis and identification of gender issues were made based on the existing data and stakeholder remarks during their participation. Along with careful planning and consideration of various factors, including sustainability, accessibility, and affordability, the proposed academic building will serve as a valuable infrastructure not only for Bukidnon State University but also for the community. The academic building features high ceilings in its classrooms to maximize the entry of natural light, creating a bright and spacious learning environment. This architectural feature not only reduces reliance on artificial lighting, thereby saving energy, but also enhances the overall ambiance of the classroom, making it more conducive to learning. Studies have shown that natural light has a positive impact on students' concentration, productivity, and well-being, making this design choice a crucial factor in fostering an effective academic atmosphere. In addition to optimizing natural light, the building incorporates a passive cooling
system through the installation of awning windows and ventilation louvers. Thesefeatures allow natural airflow to circulate within the classrooms, reducing indoor heatand minimizing the need for mechanical cooling systems such as air conditioning. Byleveraging the natural environment, this design helps maintain a comfortable indoortemperature, a crucial factor in tropical climates. Not only does this system contribute tosustainability by lowering energy consumption, but it also enhances air quality, providing a healthier environment for students and faculty.

column4: Completion of 5-Storey Academic Building-Phase 2, Quezon Campus
column6:
The second phase creation of an academic building aims to fulfill the pressing requirement of accommodating a greater student population. The inclusion of supplementary classrooms, lecture halls, and study areas on campus serves to enhance the educational experience for a varied and growing student body, ensuring the delivery of a superior level of education. The 5-storey academic building phase-2 has an estimated total cost of Php50,000,000.00. It covers about 691.74 square meters of floor area and has six (6) classrooms, having 72 square meters of floor area that could accommodate 45 students. Moreover, innovative, and green architectural designs were also integrated to the building ensuring its resiliency and sustainability for years to come. The building’s academic classrooms have high-ceilings to provide an ample natural light in the rooms creating a more ambient environment for learning. Additionally, by installing awning windows and creating cooling louvers in the classroom, a natural cooling system can be achieved as it takes advantage of the natural environment of the location. Additionally, the project features a water catchment cistern and solar panels to provide nighttime electricity for the building. It also complies with DRRCA regulations, incorporating emergency exits, fire alarms, sprinklers, and evacuation signage.

The last 3 years, there is an increase of men and women population in the campus which signifies that there is need to construct academic buildings. This will provide the male and female student of BukSU-Quezon campus to safe, affordable, accessible and conducive to learning which improves their learning capacity. The significant increase in male enrollment by 28.89% and female enrollment by 28.13% at Quezon campus for the last 3 years compared from the enrollment of the first and second semesters of SY: 2023-2024 underscores the urgent need for additional classroom space to accommodate the growing student population. This surge in enrollment reflects a broader trend of rising educational demand, necessitating infrastructure improvements to enhance the campus’s capacity. The lack of resources and infrastructure in schools affects the quality of education that students receive. Without proper facilities, students may not be able to attend classes regularly, or they may be distracted by external factors, making it difficult for them to concentrate on their studies. With the increased population for both men and women, and with the existing facilities, it cannot cater to the increased population of the present and future students of the campus, Therefore, there is a lack of learning facilities in the satellite campus. Moreover, diversity and inclusivity are the core of the institution’s values. Thus, the proposed academic building will integrate designs inspired by the rich tapestry of Bukidnon culture which symbolizes our dedication to diversity. Incorporating local cultural elements in the building design will create an inclusive and inspiring learning space for our community. In addition, environmental sustainability is a priority.  The building will feature energy-efficient systems, such as LED lighting, and advanced insulation, reducing our ecological footprint and long-term operational costs.

The completion of the 5-storey academic building includes several components such as the completion of its structural, and roofing which are essential in order for the project to perform its function as accessory in delivering quality education to the students. If the project will be completed, it will be usable and would cater the first floor six (6) classrooms.

column4: Completion of 3-Storey Dormitory, Malitbog Campus
column6:
In response to the urgent need for secure and supportive housing, especially for female students who often face heightened safety concerns, the concept of a dormitory facility was developed. This innovative project not only offers private, secure living spaces that allow students to concentrate on their academic pursuits but also actively challenges traditional gender roles that have historically limited their progress. By integrating thoughtful design features and dedicated amenities tailored to the unique needs of female students, the facility creates an environment where safety, privacy, and academic development go hand in hand. The design of the building is based upon the existing data and stakeholder remarks during the conduct of gender analysis and identification of gender issues. Both male and female participants from different beneficiary groups contributed to problem identification and project design, with the process grounded in gender analysis to address gender-specific issues. Feedback gathered during stakeholder consultations emphasized the urgent need for a female student dormitory.

At present, the construction of the dormitory building has advanced significantly, with structural works completed up to the second floor. The reinforced concrete framework, including columns, beams, and slabs, has been fully cast and cured in accordance with the approved structural design and specifications. A total of sixteen (16) dormitory rooms have been constructed, capable of accommodating sixty-four (64) female students. Ancillary facilities such as the laundry area, bathrooms, kitchen, and comfort rooms have also been constructed and are undergoing finishing works. The figure below shows the construction progress and work status of the dormitory project. Based on the current progress, the dormitory project still requires the completion of its third-floor facilities, which will include the installation of the roofing system, construction of stairways, and the addition of eight (8) dormitory rooms, along with laundry areas, comfort rooms, bathrooms, and a kitchen. The succeeding construction phase will likewise cover the development of common spaces such as the lobby and study areas to enhance the living and learning experience of resident students.

To achieve full completion, architectural finishing works and façade treatments must also be undertaken to ensure both structural integrity and aesthetic quality. Additionally, slope protection and mitigation work around the dormitory site are necessary to maintain soil stability and safeguard the surrounding terrain. The project therefore proposes an investment of 20 million to complete the remaining works. Once fully completed, the 162-square-meter dormitory will feature a total of twenty-four (24) standard rooms, providing safe and comfortable accommodation for ninety-six (96) female students, in line with Bukidnon State University’s commitment to gender-responsive, inclusive, and student-centered campus facilities.

column6:
The Nutrition Building for the Underserved and Networking (NutriBUN) Project is a multi-sectoral initiative aimed at addressing the alarming rates of poverty, food insecurity, and malnutrition in Northern Mindanao. In 2021, the poverty incidence in Region X was 26.1%, with 1.32 million individuals living below the poverty threshold and 73.6 thousand families unable to meet basic food needs. As of 2023, 4.8% of families in the region remain food poor, with Lanao del Norte experiencing the highest subsistence incidence at 11.1%.
The project integrates school-based nutrition programs, nutritional literacy, and sustainable agricultural practices to mitigate food insecurity and malnutrition while fostering community resilience. This initiative aligns with the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) goals of inclusive growth, as well as the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), and SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being).

column4: Renovation and Upgrading of CET Teaching and Learning Facilities
column6: The College of Engineering and Technology (CET) is one of the top performing colleges in the Visayas State University, Baybay City, Leyte, and also recognized as the leading institution in the Visayas and Mindanao in the fields of agricultural engineering, geodetic engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, computer science and technology, and meteorology. The college offers six (6) degree programs namely; Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering, Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Technology, Bachelor of Science in Geodetic Engineering, Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, and Bachelor of Science in Meteorology. Since its establishment, the college has produced graduates who have excelled on licensure examinations. CET aims to 1) produce globally competent graduates by providing students excellent instructions through updated curriculum; functional and state-of-the art facilities; and qualified, well-trained, and dedicated faculty and staff; 2) generate new and advance knowledge and technology in engineering and allied science through the conduct of relevant researches that can contribute towards sustainable development, climate change mitigation, food security, and advance knowledge in sciences; and 3) engage in need-based community/stakeholder projects that can make the Philippines and even the world a better place to live in. At present, two of its degree programs are accredited by the Washington Accord – the only international accreditation body for engineering academic degree programs which evaluates the program objectives, students and student outcomes, faculty and support staff, curriculum, facilities and learning environment, leadership and institutional support, extension services and linkages, including the continuity of quality improvement. Likewise, except the newly offered BS Meteorology, the five (5) academic programs are also accredited by the Accrediting Agency of Chartered Colleges and Universities in the Philippines which evaluates the mission, goals and objectives; faculty, curriculum and instruction, students, research, extension services, library, physical facilities, laboratories, and administration. Despite of the excellent reputation of CET, there is still a need to improve its facilities and learning environment to provide more effective instruction. In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic presents additional challenges not only to the students in understanding the lessons in engineering sciences, mathematics, and professional courses, but also to instructors handling such subjects online. Hence, the goal of the project is to make class delivery more participatory and efficient by transforming traditional classrooms into smart classrooms setup. A Smart Classroom is defined as a classroom that is equipped with computer and audio-visual equipment allowing the teacher to teach utilizing a range of media (Malik & Shanwal, 2015). Smart classrooms are found to be more effective than traditional setup because it develops curiosity, interest, and interactions among students and instructors (Lu et al., 2021). column4: Establishment of ICT Hub
column5: Northwestern Mindanao State College of Science and Technology
column6:
Rationale
The ICT Hub will house learning and training facilities of the 4 higher education programs of the NMSCST’s College of Information and Communications Technology (CICT):
a. 8 laboratories for computing research, and learning and training facilities for the design, development and testing of computer applications; 
b. 1 store space to pilot-test students’ entrepreneurial projects and innovation ventures; and,
c. 10 rooms for lecture classes, research and collaborative work spaces, shared office spaces for faculty and visiting experts, and administration facility of the campus computer network.

Integrated into the Hub is the campus cabling infrastructure for telecommunications and internet connectivity.

Construction will be in 3 phases, each costing 45,000,000, for a total project cost of 135,000,000.

Impact
Improved Access to Information and Resources: 
An ICT Hub provides students and faculty with immediate access to vast digital libraries, online databases, academic journals, and multimedia content, enriching the learning experience.

Flexible and Personalized Learning:
It facilitates online courses, blended learning models, and self-paced learning, allowing students to learn at their own convenience and tailor their education to their individual needs.

Increased Operational Efficiency:
Automation of routine tasks like student registration, attendance tracking, financial management, and record-keeping reduces administrative burden, saves time, and improves accuracy.

Expansion of Educational Opportunities:
ICT enables the university to offer distance learning programs and cater to a wider audience, including non-traditional students.

Cost-Effectiveness:
While there are upfront costs, ICT can lead to long-term cost efficiencies through reduced paper consumption, automated processes, and the ability to reach a larger student body on- and off-site.

This development contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly Goal 4 (Quality Education) and Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), by ensuring that education is inclusive, equitable, and of high quality. column4: Establishment of the Student Center and Residence Hall, (USTP Oroquieta), (Phase 1 and Phase 2) (Formerly: Establishment of Student Residences, (USTP  Oroquieta), (Phase 1 and Phase 2))
column5: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines
column6:
The University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines (USTP) Oroquieta Campus, located in a predominantly rural setting, faces a significant challenge in meeting the housing needs of its students. Many students commute from distant locations, placing considerable financial and logistical strain on them and their families. To address this issue, the university is establishing the Student Center and Residence Hall, a modern, cost-effective, and inclusive housing facility designed to enhance student well-being and academic success.

The proposed three-story residence will have a total floor area of 1,485.59 square meters and accommodate a minimum of 72 students. Each floor will be equipped with thoughtfully designed spaces to cater to the diverse needs of residents. These include:

Dining areas, which can also serve as shared study spaces to foster collaboration and learning, Service areas for meal preparation, ensuring convenience for students who prefer self-catering options, Utility areas, including mechanical and electrical rooms, to ensure smooth operations and maintenance of the facility.

The Student Residences reflect USTP's commitment to delivering accessible, inclusive, and sustainable education. By alleviating the burden of long commutes, the facility will enable students to focus on their academic pursuits, improving their overall quality of life. Furthermore, it will support the USTP Framework 2030, which emphasizes infrastructure development to meet student needs while promoting academic excellence and innovation.

The project aligns with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) and the Regional Development Investment Plan (RDIP) by contributing to equitable access to education, especially in rural areas. It also supports the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly: Goal 4 (Quality Education): By ensuring students have access to a conducive learning environment; and Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities): By creating sustainable and resilient housing solutions. 

The design of the Student Center and Residence Hall integrates climate-resilient and sustainable features, ensuring that the infrastructure can withstand environmental challenges. Energy-efficient systems, inclusive amenities, and robust construction techniques will be employed to minimize the environmental impact and operational costs.

In line with Gender and Development (GAD) principles, the facility will provide inclusive accommodations that meet the needs of all students, regardless of gender or background. By fostering a supportive and respectful living environment, the Student Residences will contribute to a sense of community and inclusivity within the USTP Oroquieta Campus.

The establishment of the Student Center and Residence Hall aligns with USTP’s 8-Point Agenda, focusing on enhancing student services and improving the university’s infrastructure. It also supports the university's efforts toward internationalization by providing accommodations that meet global standards, fostering local-to-global connectivity in higher education. The facility will serve as a model for higher education institutions in rural settings, demonstrating how strategic investments in housing can enhance student outcomes.

The Student Center and Residence Hall at USTP Oroquieta represent a vital step toward achieving the university’s mission of providing accessible, quality education while addressing the unique challenges of its rural setting. By fostering a conducive living and learning environment, this project will empower students, strengthen the USTP community, and contribute to the broader goal of sustainable and inclusive development.

column4: Completion of the Marine Multi-Species Building for VSU Tolosa
column6:
This proposal on the completion of the Marine Multi-Species Hatchery (MMSH) Facility of VSU Tolosa involves completing and achieving operational readiness of the facility. This phase includes structural improvements, painting, plumbing, electrical installations, ceiling and flooring installation, the installation of laboratory tables and sinks, the provision of an aeration source for the tanks, and site development. With these enhancements, the hatchery will become a fully functional facility for aquaculture instruction, research, and extension. 
In 2021, the MMSH proposal was submitted with a proposed budget for infrastructure amounting to PhP 20,000,000.00. Within the same year, the proposal was approved; however, only PhP 10,000,000.00 was allocated for infrastructure development. The project, funded with the approved PhP 10,000,000.00, was implemented and completed in 2022. Due to the 50% reduction from the proposed infrastructure budget, the building remains incomplete, lacking essential components such as painting, ceiling installation, electrical wiring, and water systems. Consequently, the MMSH is currently unable to operate according to its intended functions, thus this proposal.
Consultations with 8 male and 15 female faculty and staff of the Department of Fisheries (DFish), Faculty of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences, in collaboration with the Campus Planning and Development team, were conducted to ensure that the completion proposal aligns with the academic requirements of the hatchery and supports the improvement of the building. 
The hatchery will serve as a comprehensive hands-on learning facility, directly benefiting 130 male and 159 female students, faculty, and staff under the DFish. It will provide learning experiences in aquaculture, including broodstock and breeding management, larval rearing, nursery operations, and natural food production. The hatchery operations will integrate with specialized laboratories, including Fish Health, Phycology, Molecular Biology, and Analytical. 
The facility will also serve as an Aquaculture Research and Development Center, supporting R&D in aquaculture. Students, faculty, and other stakeholders of all genders will conduct research that focuses on breeder development, larval survival, and nursery culture techniques for marine species of high local and commercial value. 
With the university’s mandate for community engagement, the hatchery will serve as a Technology Demonstration and Training Center for fisherfolk, coastal communities, students, and other stakeholders of all genders. Extension activities will include capacity-building programs such as technical training, skills workshops, livelihood projects, and field demonstrations. The hatchery will act as a link between academic research and community application.
The project upholds Republic Act 9710, or the Magna Carta of Women, by ensuring gender-responsive approaches in instruction, research, and extension. Equal access and opportunities will be provided for both men and women in aquaculture training or in instruction, scientific research, and extension programs. In compliance with Republic Act 11313, or the Safe Spaces Act, the project commits to fostering a safe and inclusive environment for students, faculty, staff, and other beneficiaries by ensuring that all training, laboratory, and extension activities are free from gender-based harassment and discrimination.
When the hatchery becomes fully functional, it will adopt the principles of the Philippine Green Building Code, ensuring that the facility operates with (1) Energy efficiency, (2) Water conservation, (3) Proper water management, (4) Material sustainability, (5) Indoor environmental quality.
The project aims to establish the Marine Multi-Species Hatchery as a fully operational facility that supports aquaculture instruction, research, and extension by providing hands-on learning, advancing scientific studies, and delivering training and livelihood opportunities to both male and female students, faculty, staff, fisherfolk, and other beneficiaries. 
Structural and Facility Improvement
Space tables for faculty in charge
Laboratory and Hatchery equipment, aeration systems, water pumps,  
Furniture and fixtures such as office tables, chairs, storage cabinets/shelves, reception table/desk
Other supplies, such as internet access
Safety equipment such as fire extinguishers, emergency exit signs, emergency lights, first aid kits, CCTV system

These cutting-edge laboratories will provide hands-on learning experiences, enabling students to explore and innovate within their fields. The SMART Academic Building at USTP Jasaan will be a vital part of the university's mission to provide high-quality, future-focused education. The building's design incorporates flexibility, functionality, and sustainability, ensuring that it supports both academic growth and the dynamic needs of students and faculty. This project aligns with the university's Framework 2030, which prioritizes innovation, technological advancement, and the empowerment of students to contribute to both local and global challenges. This initiative is also in line with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) and the Regional Development Investment Program (RDIP), which emphasize the importance of building the skills and capacities necessary for sustainable economic growth, industrial competitiveness, and the creation of jobs. The SMART Academic Building embodies USTP's commitment to its 2030 Vision, which includes providing accessible, inclusive, and high-quality education, supporting research and innovation, and strengthening its role as a leader in higher education and technological advancement. The university’s Eight-Point Agenda emphasizes the importance of industry-academia collaboration, fostering entrepreneurship, and producing graduates who are not only capable of excelling in existing industries but are also equipped to create new industries that contribute to national and global economic growth.

In conclusion, the SMART Academic Building at USTP Jasaan is a vital step towards enhancing the university's academic offerings, advancing research and innovation, and meeting the needs of both students and the regional economy. column4: Slope / Flood Control Protection OMSC Campus Wide
column6:
The "Slope / Flood Control Protection OMSC Campus Wide" project involves the implementation of engineering and environmental measures to mitigate the risks posed by landslides, soil erosion, and flooding within the Occidental Mindoro State College (OMSC) campus. This may include activities such as:

* **Slope stabilization measures:** 
    * Construction of retaining walls, gabions, and other engineered structures to prevent slope failures. 
    * Implementation of soil bioengineering techniques, such as planting vegetation to stabilize slopes. 
* **Flood control measures:** 
    * Construction of drainage channels and culverts to improve water flow and prevent flooding. 
    * Installation of flood barriers and other flood protection structures. 
* **Erosion control measures:** 
    * Implementation of erosion control measures such as terracing, contour farming, and mulching to minimize soil loss. 
* **Environmental impact assessment and mitigation:** 
    * Conducting environmental impact assessments to identify potential environmental impacts and develop mitigation measures.

The project aims to create a safer and more resilient campus environment for students, faculty, and staff, while also protecting valuable campus infrastructure and minimizing the environmental impact of erosion and sedimentation.

column4: Construction of Industrial Academic Building - Phase 3
column5: Northwestern Mindanao State College of Science and Technology
column6:
Rationale
The College of Engineering and Technology (CET) continues to be the most populated academic unit in NMSCST, with a total of 1,877 students as of last year, accounting for approximately 30.37% of the institution’s overall college population. This significant concentration of students has led to persistent challenges in instructional space, laboratory access, and overall carrying capacity, particularly affecting the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Technology (BSIndTech) program, which offers five major fields of specialization.

Despite its growing enrollment, the BSIndTech program remains constrained by limited infrastructure, relying on shared or temporary classrooms and laboratories that hinder the full implementation of its outcomes-based curriculum. The construction of the Industrial Academic Building, which began in 2023, represents a strategic response to this growing concern. Details of the funding and implementation history of the project are as follows:

Phase 1, funded by NMSCST with ₱7,979,332.00, was completed in 2023 and served as the foundation for the building.

Phase 2, also funded by NMSCST with ₱25,000,000.00, is currently ongoing with about 25% completion as of this writing.

Phase 3, with a proposed budget of ₱50,000,000.00, aims to complete the second and third floors, including 9 classrooms and 4 laboratories, 4 comfort rooms, and a roof deck.

The completion of Phase 3 is crucial in addressing the worsening space deficiency and will significantly enhance the quality of teaching and learning for Industrial Technology and related programs. By providing dedicated and modern facilities, the new building will not only alleviate overcrowding but also enable specialized and hands-on training aligned with industry standards.

Ultimately, this infrastructure project is vital to sustaining CET’s academic excellence, accommodating its increasing student population, and meeting national goals for producing highly competent and skilled graduates in the industrial and technology sectors.

Implementation Mechanism
The implementation of Phase 3 of the Industrial Academic Building will follow a structured and transparent process to ensure timely completion, quality outputs, and efficient use of the allocated ₱50,000,000.00. The following mechanisms will be observed:
Project Planning and Coordination
A detailed project implementation plan will be developed by the Planning and Development Office, in coordination with the College of Engineering and Technology and the BSindTech program. This includes architectural and engineering designs, construction schedules, and site preparation.

Bidding and Procurement Process
In accordance with RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), the project will undergo competitive bidding. A BAC (Bids and Awards Committee) will oversee the procurement of a qualified contractor, ensuring transparency, fairness, and compliance with government standards.

Monitoring and Supervision
Weekly coordination meetings and site visits will be conducted to ensure that the project remains on schedule and within budget.

Compliance with Building and Safety Standards
All construction works will adhere to the National Building Code of the Philippines, safety regulations, and local ordinances. Third-party inspections may be conducted to ensure structural integrity and occupational safety.

Final Inspection and Turnover
Upon completion, a final inspection and evaluation will be conducted to ensure the project meets the approved specifications and standards. After which, a formal turnover ceremony will be held to transfer the building to the end-user of the College of Engineering and Technology.

Impact of the Project
The completion of Phase 3 of the Industrial Academic Building will bring significant and long-lasting impacts on the academic operations and overall institutional development of NMSCST, particularly the College of Engineering and Technology (CET). The following are the key areas of impact:
1.	Improved Learning Environment
The provision of 9 modern classrooms, 4 laboratories and 4 comfort rooms will decongest existing facilities and create a more conducive, safe, and productive learning environment. This will allow for better student engagement, hands-on training, and enhanced delivery of outcomes-based education.
2.	Enhanced Program Implementation
With dedicated spaces for instruction and laboratory work, the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Technology (BSindTech) program can fully implement its specialized curricula across its five major fields. This will elevate academic quality and help meet CHED and industry standards.
3.	Increased Student Accommodation Capacity
By expanding available facilities, the college can accommodate more enrollees, supporting institutional efforts to respond to rising demand in technology and industrial education without compromising quality.
4.	Support for Accreditation and Quality Assurance
The availability of appropriate and well-equipped infrastructure directly supports program accreditation and compliance with quality assurance requirements, increasing the institution's competitiveness and credibility.
5.	Faculty Development and Morale
Adequate instructional and laboratory spaces will enable faculty to deliver lessons more effectively and conduct practical sessions more efficiently, contributing to improved morale, performance, and academic output.
6.	Long-Term Institutional Growth
The project aligns with the strategic vision of NMSCST to become a leading institution in science and technology education. The completed building serves as a foundation for future expansions and collaborations with industry stakeholders.

column4: Establishment of Knowledge, Innovation, Science, and Technology (KIST) Park in MSU-General Santos for Commercial Agri-Fisheries R&D: Phase I-Masterplan Development

With the aim of equipping and transforming Filipino workers into highly skilled, globally competitive individuals, Mindanao State University - General Santos (MSU GenSan) prioritizes the pivotal role of the Knowledge, Innovation, Science, and Technology (KIST) Park in digitizing and driving the economy of the Philippines, particularly in Southern Mindanao. The KIST Park is an ecozone situated within the 
campuses of State Colleges and Universities (SUCs). Its purpose is to offer necessary courses required by various industries, ensuring that the academic institutions meet the skills and job demands of these industries.

It will also facilitate the transfer of university knowledge to businesses, encourage the development of faculty and student-led spin-offs, and promote the creation of innovative products and processes. 

Additionally, the KIST Park aims to promote industrial research and development, attract foreign investments in high value-added activities, and transition the country from a labor intensive economy to a knowledge-intensive one. 

MSU GenSan takes the lead in providing educational and research excellence, particularly in the agri-fisheries sector, which plays a vital role in the socio-economic development of Mindanao. The university's faculty in science, technology, agriculture, fisheries, engineering, social sciences, education, and business administration all contribute to the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem. column4: CONSTRUCTION OF FOUR-STOREY ACADEMIC BUILDING WITH ROOF DECK - Phase I
column5: Mindanao State University -Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography
column6:
The proposed project involves the construction of a four-storey academic building with a roof deck at MSU-TCTO. This infrastructure aims to respond to the university’s increasing enrollment, the introduction of new degree programs, and the need for more functional academic spaces. Each of the four floors will have seven classrooms and two gender-specific toilet facilities, while the roof deck will provide an open space for student activities, future expansions, or utility installations. The building will serve as the academic home for four colleges: the College of Business, Accountancy, and Management, the College of Mathematical Sciences, and the College of Engineering, in line with CHED’s recommendation to group programs by discipline into distinct colleges.

This project will provide a modern, safe, and accessible learning environment that supports high-quality instruction, research, and extension services. It will also improve institutional compliance with national higher education standards and contribute to MSU-TCTO’s long-term development goals. With a total floor area of approximately 3,582.236 square meters, the building will strengthen the university’s capacity to deliver future-ready, inclusive, and globally aligned education while supporting sustainable infrastructure development under both regional and national policy frameworks.

This infrastructure project is the Phase I of the proposed three-phase Academic Complex, which will consolidate all colleges into an integrated facility to maximize space efficiency and enable a smart, green campus. The project is aligned with globally recognized sustainability and performance frameworks, including LEED for holistic green building design and operations (energy, water, materials, waste, and indoor environmental quality), IFC/EDGE for measurable resource-efficiency targets (minimum 20% savings in energy, water, and materials/embodied impacts), and WELL for health- and well-being-focused building outcomes. The project also supports institutional sustainability through ISO 14001 (environmental management systems) and ISO 50001 (energy management systems), while adopting internationally used energy-efficiency baselines such as ASHRAE Standard 90.1 and relevant local green building assessment pathways such as the 2015 Green Building of the Philippines.

column4: CONSTRUCTION OF THREE-STOREY COLLEGE OF INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY BUILDING 2 AT MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1
column6:
Catanduanes State University's College of Information and Communications technology (CICT) emerged from the university's commitment to bridging the digital divide and promoting information technology (IT) for academic and societal progress. Its roots can be traced back to the late 1980s, when IT began to be integrated into existing programs within the College of Business and Accounting. Over time, it formally evolved as a separate college, transitioning from the Computer Technology Department (CTD). Dedicated faculty and visionary leaders like Dr. Gabriel Rodolfo and Mr. Exequiel A. Mariano Jr., played a pivotal role in this development.
	
In 2008, CICT was merged with the College of Industrial Technology and College of Engineering to form the College of Technology (COT) as part of a university restructuring. However, recognizing the growing importance of ICT, the university re-established CICT as a separate college in 2015, allowing focused development and course offerings.

Catanduanes State University (CatSU), as the premier higher education institution in the province, continues to respond to the growing demands for quality Information and Communications Technology (ICT) education. The College of Information and Communications Technology (CICT) has emerged as one of the most dynamic and rapidly growing academic units of the university, offering programs such as Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (BSIT), Information Systems (BSIS), Computer Science (BSCS), Library and Information Science (BLIS), and Entertainment and Multimedia Computing (BSEMC).

From academic year 2021–2022 to 2023–2024, CICT has recorded a remarkable 38% increase in student enrollment, a trend expected to continue given the growing demand for ICT professionals both locally and globally. This growth reflects the increasing relevance of digital skills in today’s society, and underscores the urgent need for CatSU to strengthen its capacity to deliver high-quality ICT education.

Despite this growth and the high priority classification of CICT programs in the university’s academic offerings, the current CICT building remains severely inadequate. The existing infrastructure houses a limited number of classrooms and computer laboratories, which are shared not only by CICT students but also by students from other colleges enrolled in IT-related general education or service courses. This has resulted in overcrowded classrooms, extended class schedules, and competition for limited laboratory resources, thereby affecting the quality and delivery of instruction.

In fact, among all academic colleges within the university, CICT is the only unit that has not yet been given significant infrastructure expansion, despite accounting for 13% of the total university enrollment under priority programs. This disparity significantly hampers the College’s ability to meet its instructional, research, and extension mandates. More critically, it restricts the university’s ability to respond to the rapid pace of technological advancement and to produce ICT graduates who are equipped with industry-relevant competencies.

The proposed Construction of a Three-Storey CICT Building 2 is intended to directly address these long-standing constraints by providing additional and purpose-built academic spaces — including lecture halls, computer laboratories, innovation rooms, faculty offices, and collaborative learning areas. These new facilities will not only ease congestion in the existing building but will also enable the College to introduce new program offerings and adopt emerging technologies aligned with the evolving ICT landscape.

This infrastructure project has been consistently identified as a strategic priority in the university’s Annual Operational Plan (AOP) and is crucial to ensuring that CatSU remains responsive to regional development goals, national workforce requirements, and global trends in digital transformation.

Without immediate intervention, the College may face the possibility of limiting student admissions, adversely impacting the university’s institutional targets, and hindering its contribution to local and national development through the production of highly skilled ICT professionals. An urgent investment in infrastructure is therefore essential to sustain academic excellence, accommodate increasing student populations, and maintain the relevance of CatSU’s ICT programs in the years to come.

The project will support the delivery of STEM-aligned degree programs by integrating dedicated spaces for physics, chemistry, biology, and other scientific disciplines, equipped with the necessary utilities, safety systems, and instrumentation to facilitate safe, effective, and outcomes-based laboratory instruction.

The facility is designed to meet the increasing demand for hands-on, inquiry-based learning and will enable the university to fully implement the outcomes-based education (OBE) framework. From a national development perspective, the project directly supports the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, particularly the sector outcome of Enhanced Quality and Access to Education and Accelerated Human Capital Development. It will strengthen CatSU’s capability to produce graduates with strong technical competencies, thereby contributing to the country’s goal of cultivating a skilled, innovation-oriented workforce. In parallel, the facility will enhance the university’s capacity to undertake research and development (R&D), complementing the PDP’s call for Technology-Driven Innovation through increased investments in science education infrastructure.

column4: CONSTRUCTION OF THREE-STOREY COLLEGE OF LAW BUILDING AT MAIN CAMPUS
column6:
Access to justice—the ability of individuals to seek and obtain remedies through formal or informal justice institutions in accordance with international human rights standards—is fundamental to an inclusive and equitable society. However, the World Justice Project 2018 Survey revealed that only 20% of Filipinos were able to access legal help, with 72% relying on friends and family, 15% seeking assistance from lawyers, and the rest turning to institutions. This situation reflects a significant gap in legal service delivery, particularly among the poor and marginalized sectors.

In the province of Catanduanes, the problem is similarly pronounced due to the limited number of law practitioners. To help address this issue, the Provincial Government enacted Provincial Ordinance No. 015-2021, otherwise known as the “Catanduanes Medicine and Law Scholarship Program Ordinance,” which provides scholarships and a return service program to support deserving students in pursuing law and medical degrees—while ensuring the future availability of these professionals to serve the province.

In response to this local need, Catanduanes State University (CatSU)—the only government-run institution of higher learning in the province—takes on the responsibility of offering relevant curricular programs as mandated under Section 4 of Republic Act 10229. In line with this mandate, CatSU introduced its Juris Doctor (J.D.) program, designed to contribute to the development of future legal professionals who can uphold justice, influence policy, and support underserved communities. The program offers a multi-disciplinary learning approach that hones students’ research and communication skills, critical to the practice of law. Backed by a dedicated and outstanding corps of faculty, the J.D. program aims to fully prepare a select group of students for the Bar exams through hands-on mentoring and rigorous academic training.

column4: RELOCATION AND REHABILITATION OF COVERT COURT AT CATSU MAIN CAMPUS
column6:
The former covered court of the Catanduanes State University (CatSU) Main Campus, situated at the rear of the Main Administration Building, historically functioned as a multipurpose facility supporting a wide range of university and community activities, including sports, cultural events, assemblies, and outreach programs. In 2020, Typhoon Rolly—classified as one of the most intense tropical cyclones to strike the Philippines—inflicted severe structural damage. The extreme wind loads and heavy precipitation compromised the roof sheeting, primary and secondary steel framing, and vertical support elements, while prolonged exposure to moisture accelerated the deterioration of the playing surface. Structural assessments rendered the facility unsafe for occupancy and recommended full reconstruction or replacement.

As part of the university’s strategic infrastructure planning, the Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP) was updated to integrate priority projects that address both academic and climate-resilience objectives. In this process, the original covered court site was repurposed for the construction of a water catchment basin, owing to its naturally depressed topography and high water-retention capacity. This intervention addresses a critical climate adaptation measure for CatSU, ensuring sustainable rainwater harvesting to support irrigation, sanitation, and other non-potable water needs, thus reducing operational water costs and contributing to environmental sustainability.

As per the prior year of budget cycle, this project was classified as “uncategorized” by DEPDev (formerly NEDA) as it represents a disaggregated component of what would typically form part of a larger campus sports and wellness infrastructure program. However, the relocation and reconstruction of the covered court are directly tied to a broader institutional vision of developing a complete Sports Complex within the main campus. The disaggregation in this instance is justified by the urgency of restoring the covered court’s functionality as a standalone high-demand facility, while the remainder of the Sports Complex will follow in separate phases based on funding availability and program readiness.

Prior to site repurposing, recoverable steel members—including I-beams, trusses, purlins, and steel plates—were dismantled and stored under controlled conditions to prevent corrosion and material fatigue. These salvaged components will undergo quality inspection, sandblasting, and protective coating before integration into the new covered court structure. The facility will be constructed at the designated Sports Complex zone within the campus, where it will be integrated with other athletic and wellness infrastructure. The design will incorporate higher wind load resistance, improved foundation anchorage, and upgraded roofing systems compliant with the latest National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP) and the Building Code of the Philippines.

Upon completion, the new covered court will restore a critical venue for academic, extracurricular, and community events, directly contributing to the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028 sector outcome of “Enhanced Access to Quality Education and Lifelong Learning Opportunities” under the Human Capital Development pillar. By providing a safe, climate-resilient, and multi-use facility, the project supports youth development, wellness promotion, and community engagement, while optimizing the use of government resources through material recycling and climate-adaptive site planning.
