column4: Establishment of Agriculture, Fisheries & Aquatic Sciences - Academic Infrastructure for Learning and Enhanced Spaces (AFAS-AILES) Project
column6:
The AFAS-AILES Project is a comprehensive academic infrastructure development program designed to modernize and expand the instructional spaces of Southern Leyte State University – Bontoc Campus, particularly for its flagship programs in Agriculture, Fisheries, and Marine Biology. The program consists of four major infrastructure components: (1) Construction of a Two-Storey Learning Spaces Building with Integrated Mini Theater, (2) Construction of Green Academic Learning Spaces for the Fisheries Program, (3) Construction of Green Academic Learning Spaces for the Marine Biology Program, and (4) Construction of Green Academic Learning Buildings for the Agriculture Program. Together, these sub-projects provide discipline-specific, inclusive, energy-efficient, and future-ready learning environments that will address the critical instructional capacity gaps of the campus.

1. Construction of Two-Storey Learning Spaces with Integrated Mini Theater 

The Two-Storey Learning Spaces Building with Integrated Mini Theater will function as a modern learning hub with six contemporary classrooms, a designated faculty space, and an integrated mini theater designed for lectures, cultural presentations, seminars, and community-engagement activities. The facility is intended for students who are taking up programs related to aquatic and applied life sciences (e.g., Marine Biology, Fisheries, Agriculture/Aquaculture). This building enhances academic delivery by creating flexible learning areas that support advanced teaching strategies, collaborative learning, and enrichment programs. Accessibility features—including ramps, wide corridors, and gendered plus gender-neutral comfort rooms—ensure that the facility supports inclusive and equitable learning for all students.

2. Construction of Green Academic Learning Spaces for Fisheries program 

The Green Academic Learning Spaces for the Fisheries Program consists of a solar-powered academic building designed with seven flexible lecture rooms and a faculty office. It will incorporate universal design standards such as PWD-accessible restrooms, ramps, and signage, along with energy-efficient systems that reduce operational costs and environmental impact. This facility will provide the Fisheries program with purpose-built learning environments aligned with laboratory-based, hands-on, and field-integrated instruction essential to the discipline.

3. Construction of Green Academic Learning Spaces for Marine Biology program 

Similarly, the Green Academic Learning Spaces for the Marine Biology Program will provide specialized learning environments for marine science instruction. The seven lecture rooms and dedicated faculty office in each structure will support the program’s growing enrollment and academic requirements, particularly for applied sciences and laboratory-intensive courses. The building will also incorporate solar energy systems, natural lighting, and ventilation, contributing to climate action and sustainable campus operations.

4. Construction of Green Academic Learning Spaces for Agriculture program 
The Green Academic Learning Spaces for the Agriculture Program represent the largest component of the project. Each Agriculture building will include seven lecture rooms and a faculty office, all equipped with sustainability features and PWD-accessible facilities. These structures will directly support theoretical, laboratory-based, and field-integrated instruction central to agricultural sciences, enabling SLSU–Bontoc to expand its academic offerings, strengthen outcomes-based education, and improve alignment with industry standards and regional workforce needs.

Collectively, the AFAS-AILES Project responds to pressing infrastructure deficiencies in the campus—specifically, the lack of modern classrooms, outdated instructional spaces, and insufficient facilities for applied agricultural and aquatic sciences. By constructing three (3) new academic buildings with universal design and renewable-energy features, the program enhances instructional capacity, facilitates research and practical training, and promotes sustainability in alignment with national policies and global development frameworks.

The project contributes directly to several priority outcomes under the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028 Results Matrix, including:

• Improved access to quality education and lifelong learning through expanded and modern instructional facilities;

• Infrastructure modernization and resilience through the construction of sustainable, inclusive, and energy-efficient academic buildings;

• Enhanced agricultural productivity and innovation by developing facilities that support agriculture-related training and research; and

• Accelerated energy transition and climate action through the adoption of solar-powered and green building features.

It also aligns with the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan (RDP) and RDIP, which emphasize agricultural development, sustainable higher education facilities, expanded access to science-based programs, and environmentally resilient infrastructure systems.
Through its integrated approach to infrastructure expansion, inclusivity, sustainability, and academic strengthening, the AFAS-AILES Project will significantly elevate the instructional capability, research potential, and community engagement capacity of SLSU–Bontoc Campus—positioning it as a key contributor to regional human capital development in agriculture, fisheries, and aquatic sciences.

column4: Establishment of Integrated Sustainable Agricultural Genomics and Advanced Research Innovation Complex Support System (EIS-AGRARICoSS)
column6:
The Establishment of Integrated Sustainable Agricultural Genomics and Advanced Research Innovation Complex Support System (EIS-AGRARICoSS) is a comprehensive, multi-component program designed to strengthen the research, innovation, and development capabilities of Southern Leyte State University–Bontoc Campus in support of agricultural modernization, food security, and climate-resilient farming systems. The program consists of two major sub-projects: (1) the Establishment of the Agricultural Genomic Research Center and (2) the Establishment of the Advanced Research Innovation Complex Support System—a three-storey integrated research building complemented by smart greenhouse infrastructure.

1. Establishment of Agricultural Genomic Research Center

The Agricultural Genomic Research Center will serve as a specialized facility dedicated to genomics-based crop improvement, molecular breeding, and biotechnology research. Its components include a molecular biology and genetics laboratory, DNA sequencing and gene expression analysis suites, a bioinformatics and data analytics laboratory, and training spaces for researchers and students. This facility will support the development of genomic databases for priority crops, marker-assisted breeding initiatives, and research on pest resistance, climate adaptation traits, and enhanced nutritional quality.

2. Establishment of Advanced Research Innovation Complex Support System

The Advanced Research Innovation Complex will house multiple laboratories critical to a modern agricultural R&D ecosystem, including an Animal Nutrition and Feed Laboratory, Soil Testing and Analysis Laboratory, Crops Disease Diagnostic Laboratory, Agronomic Seed Technology Laboratory, Crop Physiology Laboratory, and Postharvest Science Laboratory. These laboratories will enable advanced diagnostics, soil and plant health assessment, seed quality evaluation, livestock nutrition research, postharvest loss reduction, and agronomic experimentation. Smart greenhouse units equipped with automated irrigation, environmental sensors, and climate-control systems will support precision agriculture research and controlled-environment crop production trials.

Together, these facilities will function as an integrated research hub supporting outcomes aligned with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028 Results Matrix, particularly:

• PDP Chapter 4 – Transforming the Agriculture and Agrifood Systems, through enhancement of agricultural R&D, local value chain efficiency, and climate-resilient crop development;

• PDP Chapter 9 – Advancing Research, Development, and Innovation, by expanding STI infrastructure and strengthening university–industry–government partnerships;

• PDP Chapter 15 – Accelerating Climate Action and Disaster Resilience, through the development of crop varieties and farming systems adaptive to climate risks.

The purpose of constructing these government research facilities is to provide technical capacity, diagnostic services, scientific knowledge generation, and innovative agricultural solutions for farmers, researchers, LGUs, and agri-based enterprises. The laboratories will generate measurable outputs such as increased research publications, development of crop improvement tools, delivery of training programs, expanded R&D partnerships, and strengthened extension services—contributing directly to PDP-RM indicators on agricultural productivity, R&D intensity, innovation capacity, and climate-resilient development.

column4: Strategic Physical Assets for Resilient Campus (S.P.A.R.C.) Program:  Building Resilient Infrastructure for Academic Excellence and Community Impact
column6:
The Strategic Physical Assets for Resilient Campus (S.P.A.R.C.) Program is a comprehensive multi-component infrastructure initiative aimed at strengthening the resiliency, functionality, and service capacity of Southern Leyte State University–Bontoc Campus. The program integrates five major sub-projects—each addressing critical gaps in campus safety, disaster preparedness, student support services, mobility, academic engagement spaces, and energy resilience. Collectively, the S.P.A.R.C. Program modernizes campus infrastructure in alignment with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028 Results Matrix (RM), particularly goals on resilient infrastructure development, human capital development, disaster risk reduction, sustainable mobility, and clean energy transition.

1. Completion of Multi-Purpose Building, Phase II

This sub-project completes the remaining structural, architectural, electrical, plumbing, and finishing works of the Multipurpose Building (MPB). The completed facility will include a high-resolution LED wall, professional audio systems, and a full HVAC installation to support academic, cultural, research, and international engagements. Strengthened roofing and disaster-resilient features will enable the MPB to function as an auxiliary evacuation center during severe weather events. The facility will incorporate an off-grid solar power system to ensure uninterrupted operations during power outages and reduce long-term electricity costs. The MPB contributes to PDP-RM outcomes on functional and resilient learning spaces, capacity for internationalization, and community-safe infrastructure.

2. SPARC Safe Center: Integrated Student, DRRM, and Evacuation Center

The project involves constructing a two-storey center that integrates student services with disaster preparedness capabilities. The first level will contain student lounges, a canteen, study areas, an information desk, and a multi-faith prayer/reflection room. The second level will house a health and wellness hub—including a clinic and fitness center—along with a fully equipped evacuation center, relief goods storage, and an office for the DRRM Unit. The facility strengthens campus safety, enhances student well-being, and provides a dedicated crisis response hub aligned with PDP-RM indicators on DRRM capacity, health and wellness infrastructure, and inclusive learning support systems.

3. SPARC Vital Grounds: Improvement of Campus Sports Grounds and Outdoor Facility

This sub-project rehabilitates the campus oval and surrounding open spaces to create a safe, inclusive, and fully functional multipurpose sports and outdoor facility. Improvements include drainage systems, turf leveling, track and field upgrades, lighting installations, spectator stands, hygiene facilities, and fitness zones. The enhanced open space will also serve as an emergency assembly area, helicopter landing zone, and venue for large community events. These improvements support PDP-RM outcomes related to human development, sports development, community resilience, and public open space enhancement.

4. SPARC Mobility Loop: Upgrading of Campus Circumferential Road

The S.P.A.R.C. Mobility Loop upgrades the campus’s 1.6-kilometer circumferential road into a fully concreted, all-weather, climate-resilient mobility network. Improvements include integrated drainage systems, slope protection, pedestrian walkways, bicycle lanes, and PWD-friendly access points. This road network will link academic buildings, laboratories, student housing, administrative units, and income-generating facilities—addressing mobility challenges that previously caused inefficiency, safety risks, and accessibility barriers. The upgraded network supports PDP targets related to sustainable transport, mobility enhancement, and climate-adaptive infrastructure.

5. SPARC Solar Shift: Advancing Green Energy and Resilience through Renewable Infrastructure

This sub-project involves installing a 500-kW off-grid solar PV system across key academic, administrative, and support buildings. The installation includes digital monitoring systems, smart inverters, and battery energy storage solutions. By reducing dependence on grid electricity and mitigating the impacts of power interruptions, the solar shift strengthens operational continuity and campus resilience. This supports PDP-RM indicators on clean energy adoption, energy resilience, and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

The S.P.A.R.C. Program supports multiple PDP-RM outcomes, including:

• Development of climate-resilient and inclusive infrastructure (PDP Chapters 10 & 15);
• Strengthened DRRM systems for communities and institutions;
• Enhanced human capital through improved learning and wellness facilities (Chapter 4);
• Expanded access to sustainable mobility systems;
• Accelerated renewable energy adoption and reduced vulnerability to energy disruptions.

The construction of these government facilities is essential for ensuring continuity of academic operations, strengthening disaster readiness, improving student welfare, expanding institutional capacity for internationalization, and enabling safe and efficient campus mobility. Collectively, the program provides the necessary infrastructure foundation for SLSU–Bontoc Campus to fulfill its mandate for quality higher education, community service, and resilient development.

column4: RESEARCH EXCELLENCE, ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT & TRAINING EXPANSION FOR TOMAS OPPUS CAMPUS (REED-TE TOC)
column6:
The REED-TE TOC Program is a multi-component infrastructure initiative designed to elevate Tomas Oppus Campus into a regional hub for innovation, scientific research, enterprise incubation, and workforce development. It consists of three major sub-projects: (1) the Completion of the Business Incubation Building, (2) the Construction of the Research Facility for Advanced Science Studies, and (3) the Construction of a 7,570-sqm Training Center. These facilities will collectively address critical infrastructure gaps that hinder the campus’s ability to support entrepreneurship, CHED-mandated science teacher training, industry-responsive education, and technical-vocational skills development.

1. Completion  of the Construction of Business Incubation Building

The Completion of the Business Incubation Building will finalize a flagship facility envisioned to serve as the center for enterprise development, innovation research, and MSME support. The completed building will house a DTI Hub for MSME consultancy and training; a Business Incubation and Simulation Room for student-led and community ventures; a Business Information System Laboratory for Business Analytics instruction; TESDA Training and Certification spaces for skills development; modern classrooms for the growing BSBA program; an Alumni Center to strengthen industry partnerships; faculty rooms; and a conference hall for seminars and collaborative research. This facility will support capacity-building for local entrepreneurs, create pathways for inclusive economic participation, and directly strengthen the innovation ecosystem in Southern Leyte.

2. Construction of Research Facility for Advanced Science Studies

The Construction of the Research Facility for Advanced Science Studies will establish dedicated laboratories essential for high-quality science education, teacher training, and research productivity. The facility will include a Physics Laboratory, a Molecular Biology Laboratory, and an Analytical Chemistry Laboratory—enabling advanced studies in mechanics, optics, microbial biology, genetics, environmental chemistry, and water and air quality assessment. As SLSU–TOC has been designated by CHED as a training center for science teachers under the Institutional Development and Innovation Grant (IDIG), the facility will serve as the institutional backbone for delivering evidence-based science instruction, supporting pre-service and in-service teacher training, and promoting community-engaged scientific research.

3. Construction of Training Center

The Construction of the Training Center will provide a modern, 7,570-square-meter multi-functional facility for technical and vocational education, professional development programs, and community training. Its components include a 25m training pool with locker rooms, two mess halls with alfresco dining areas, a business hub, lobby and lounge with concierge, landscaped courtyard, administrative offices, classrooms, workshops, elevator, conference hall, and residential rooms for trainees. This center will deliver TESDA-aligned and industry-based training programs, enhance employability, support local workforce upskilling, and provide inclusive access to disadvantaged groups, including out-of-school youth, displaced workers, and women in vulnerable sectors.

The REED-TE TOC Program contributes directly to priority outcomes in the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028 Results Matrix, including:

• Improved education and lifelong learning outcomes through expanded and modernized learning environments;

• Strengthened research, development, and innovation systems through dedicated science laboratories and enterprise incubation infrastructure;

• Enhanced MSME capability and competitiveness through training hubs and incubation services; and

• Accelerated human capital development and workforce productivity through the establishment of a standardized training center aligned with industry needs.
The program also aligns with the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan and the Regional Development Investment Program (RDIP) by advancing regional innovation, improving science education capacity, expanding opportunities for MSMEs, and strengthening technical-vocational training infrastructure.

By completing these facilities, the program ensures that SLSU–Tomas Oppus Campus can deliver high-impact education, foster entrepreneurial ecosystems, support national and regional innovation agendas, and provide inclusive skills development opportunities. Together, these components establish a cohesive infrastructure foundation that directly contributes to PDP-RM indicators on innovation, MSME development, human capital formation, and quality education.

column4: SLSU CARE (Campus Accommodation and Resident Experience Program)
column6:
The SLSU CARE (Campus Accommodation and Resident Experience) Program is a comprehensive student welfare and infrastructure development initiative that aims to expand and modernize the residential facilities of Southern Leyte State University to address the growing need for safe, affordable, gender-responsive, and academically supportive on-campus housing. The program consists of two major components: (1) the Completion of the Three-Storey, 30-Unit Female Dormitory (Phase II) and (2) the Construction of the Modern Male Dormitory, both designed to enhance the campus living environment and directly support student retention, well-being, and equitable educational access.

1. Completion of the Three-Storey, 30-Unit Female Dormitory (Phase II)

The first component, the Completion of the Three-Storey, 30-Unit Female Dormitory (Phase II), involves finishing the remaining construction works of the ground, second, and third floors of the facility. This dormitory is designed to house up to 240 female students and includes an information counter, receiving lobby, canteen, kitchen, mess hall, lounge, recreational area, oratory, dorm rooms, and accessible facilities for students with disabilities. Upper floors will feature residential units, wide hallways, study areas for collaborative and individual learning, and communal spaces to support psychosocial well-being and academic success. This sub-project directly contributes to PDP-RM outcomes on improved access to higher education, enhanced student welfare services, and provision of gender-responsive and inclusive education environments.

2. Elevating Campus Life: Construction of Modern Male Dormitory

The second component, the Construction of the Modern Male Dormitory, mirrors the female dormitory in design and purpose and will also accommodate up to 240 male students. The facility will include an information and receiving area, canteen, kitchen, mess hall, lounge, recreational room, oratory, accessible rooms for PWD students, and upper-floor residential units with dedicated study and common areas. By providing secure, affordable, and supportive on-campus accommodation, the male dormitory reduces reliance on costly or unsafe off-campus housing and reinforces the University's commitment to equitable learning conditions and holistic student development. This aligns with PDP-RM targets related to livable communities, safe learning environments, and human capital development.

Both infrastructures are designed with gender-responsive, inclusive, and student-centered principles, ensuring compliance with national standards on accessibility, safety, and welfare. The program directly responds to increasing student population and the limited availability of on-campus housing, which has historically affected student retention, academic performance, and safety—particularly for learners from geographically isolated barangays and low-income households. By expanding residential capacity, the SLSU CARE Program enhances the living–learning environment essential to academic success, campus engagement, and personal development.

The program strongly supports the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, specifically:

• Subchapter 2.2 Improve Education and Lifelong Learning (improving facilities that support student access and retention),

• Subchapter 2.3 Establish Livable Communities (developing safe and inclusive residential environments), and

• Chapter 12 Expand and Upgrade Infrastructure (constructing resilient, accessible, and student-centered buildings).

At the regional level, the program advances the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan and RDIP through improved higher education infrastructure, expanded student support systems, and strengthened human capital development.

By completing the female dormitory and constructing the male dormitory, the SLSU CARE Program will deliver modern, inclusive, and academically conducive residential facilities that significantly enhance the student experience and support the University’s long-term vision as a Future Perfect University.

column4: Modernization of CPSC Laboratory Equipment and Facilities for COPC
column6: Camiguin Polytechnic State College, located in Mambajao, Camiguin, envisions itself as a vibrant and empowered institution of higher learning that is accessible, globally competitive, and responsive to cultural, moral, eco-tourism, and natural resource development needs. Mandated under Section 3 of RA 7923, CPSC is tasked to provide professional, technical, and special instruction, promote research and extension services, and offer advanced studies and progressive leadership in agriculture, forestry, engineering, arts and sciences, and other relevant fields. Since its creation in 1995 through RA 7923, which integrated several former satellite campuses into one state college, CPSC has grown to become the only public higher education institution in the island province of Camiguin. Enrollment has increased from 2,890 students in AY 2020 to 4,121 in AY 2025, supported by six institutes offering fourteen programs and eighteen majors, many of which hold AACCUP accreditation and CHED Certificates of Program Compliance. Despite these achievements, the college continues to struggle with outdated laboratory equipment, insufficient facilities, and limited instructional resources, which hinder its ability to meet current industry standards and provide quality training aligned with modern technologies. As a state college with minimal tuition fees, CPSC relies on government funding and cannot independently acquire the laboratory tools and equipment required by CHED’s curriculum standards. While parents, alumni, and student organizations have contributed books, minor tools, and small improvements, the needs far exceed what local support can provide. The proposed project seeks CHED assistance to acquire modern laboratory equipment necessary for upgrading instructional facilities, improving the competency of students and faculty, supporting national certification and employability, meeting CHED minimum requirements for laboratory compliance, strengthening AACCUP accreditation performance, and ensuring that CPSC continues producing industry-ready graduates who contribute to local and national development.

column4: Comprehensive Infrastructure Expansion and Educational Advancement Program (CIEEAP) of Southern Leyte State University-San Juan Campus
column6:
The Comprehensive Infrastructure Expansion and Educational Advancement Program (CIEEAP) is a multi-component institutional development initiative that aims to modernize, expand, and climate-proof the physical infrastructure of Southern Leyte State University – San Juan Campus to support quality instruction, student welfare, sustainable operations, and community resilience. The program is composed of five major infrastructure sub-projects: (1) Construction of the Industrial Technology Building, (2) Construction of a Two-Storey Boys Dormitory Building, (3) Construction of a Two-Storey Apartment Hotel (Apartel) Building, (4) Establishing Solar Energy Infrastructure, and (5) Construction of a Sport/Evacuation Center. Each component is designed to address critical capacity gaps, improve service delivery, and support the campus’s long-term academic and socioeconomic mandates.

1. Construction of the Industrial Technology Building
 
The Industrial Technology Building will serve as the primary instructional facility for Industrial Technology and engineering-related programs, replacing aging, typhoon-damaged buildings currently used by the department. It will house specialized laboratories, lecture halls, industry-aligned equipment, and competency-based training spaces that support machining, welding, electrical systems, automotive work, electronics, and drafting. The facility will ensure the safe, modern, and industry-responsive environment necessary for hands-on technical education, skills development, and program accreditation requirements—thereby raising academic quality and supporting PDP outcomes on human capital development and workforce readiness.

2. Construction of Two-Storey Boys Dormitory Building 

The Two-Storey Boys Dormitory Building will address increasing student accommodation demands by providing safe, organized, and accessible on-campus housing for male students from distant barangays and municipalities. The facility includes furnished bedrooms, study areas, common lounges, utility rooms, and adequate restroom facilities. By offering secure and affordable accommodations, the dormitory enhances student retention, promotes academic productivity, and reduces risks associated with long-distance travel—contributing directly to PDP-RM indicators on equitable access to quality education.

3. Construction of Two-Storey Apartment Hotel (Apartel) Building 

The Two-Storey Apartment Hotel (Apartel) Building will provide guest accommodations for visiting faculty, external evaluators, training participants, and university partners. It will feature fully furnished rooms, reception and lounge areas, dining and pantry areas, and utility/service spaces. Beyond supporting academic and administrative operations, the Apartel will function as an income-generating facility consistent with SUCs’ mandate to diversify revenue sources, improve fiscal sustainability, and support regional knowledge exchange through short-term training and extension programs.

4. Establishing Solar Energy Infrastructure 

The Solar Energy Infrastructure sub-project will install photovoltaic (PV) panels, inverters, mounting structures, power conduits, and battery storage to reduce dependence on grid-supplied electricity, lower operational costs, and enhance campus energy resilience. The system will power classrooms, laboratories, administrative offices, and support buildings, contributing to climate action by reducing carbon emissions. This component aligns with PDP and RDP directives to expand renewable energy adoption, promote clean energy transitions, and support sustainable and cost-efficient operations in public institutions.

5. Construction of Sport/Evacuation Center 

The Sport/Evacuation Center is a dual-purpose facility designed to function as a sports venue during normal operations and as a designated evacuation center during disasters. It will include a covered court, spectator areas, locker rooms, comfort rooms, storage rooms, administrative spaces, and emergency facilities such as elevated flooring, emergency exits, and accessible power and water points. The Center will support intramural activities, physical education programs, community-based recreational events, and large gatherings. During calamities, the structure will serve as a safe temporary shelter equipped to accommodate evacuees efficiently. This project advances PDP-RM outcomes on disaster preparedness, resilient communities, and improved public infrastructure safety.

Collectively, the CIEEAP supports strategic national and regional development priorities under the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, specifically:

• Improved education and lifelong learning (through modern classrooms, laboratories, and student housing),

• Expanded and upgraded infrastructure (through resilient and sustainable public facilities),

• Increased renewable energy adoption (through solar power installations), and

• Strengthened disaster risk reduction and resilience (through the Sport/Evacuation Center).

It also aligns with the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan (RDP) and Regional Development Investment Program (RDIP), which prioritize resilient educational facilities, sustainable energy systems, safe student environments, and community-ready evacuation structures.

Through these integrated infrastructure investments, the CIEEAP will significantly enhance the learning environment, operational capacity, sustainability performance, and community resilience of SLSU – San Juan Campus, ensuring its continued contribution to regional human capital and socioeconomic development.

The SMART RESCUE Program is a multi-component infrastructure and modernization initiative designed to strengthen the energy security, digital capability, and disaster resilience of Southern Leyte State University – Hinunangan Campus. Located along the Pacific-facing eastern seaboard—one of the world’s most active typhoon corridors—the campus requires robust, climate-responsive systems and facilities to ensure continuity of academic operations, safeguard life and property, and support community-based emergency response. The program is composed of three major sub-projects: (1) the Green Power Initiative – Expansion of Solar Energy Facilities, (2) the Rehabilitation of the IT Building and Upgrading of ICT Infrastructure, and (3) the Construction of a Fully Equipped DRRM Center and Campus Clinic.

1. Green Power Initiative – Expansion of Solar Energy Facilities

The Green Power Initiative involves expanding the campus solar farm to a total installed capacity of 500–660 kWp, with a minimum of 1,166 high-efficiency solar panels, advanced hybrid inverters, and a 3,300Ah Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). This infrastructure will ensure stable energy supply despite frequent SOLECO outages and voltage fluctuations, while creating a functional laboratory for renewable energy research and instruction. It includes a centralized monitoring system to support academic, technical, and extension activities related to sustainable energy systems. The project directly responds to high annual power losses and equipment damage caused by grid instability, enabling academic continuity and reducing electricity expenditures.

2. Rehabilitation of IT Building and Upgrading of ICT Infrastructure

The Rehabilitation of the IT Building and Upgrading of ICT Infrastructure modernizes the existing one-storey structure into a two-storey ICT facility that meets current digital education standards. The redesigned building includes strengthened structural components, improved roofing and ventilation, LED and energy-efficient systems, BP 344 accessibility features, and a solar-ready electrical distribution network. The ICT upgrade features four computer laboratories, eight smart classrooms equipped with interactive technologies, enhanced Wi-Fi and campus network systems, RFID-based access control, secure data storage, and a Campus Information System and Analytics (CISA) Office to support cybersecurity, systems maintenance, and digital transformation initiatives. This component directly strengthens the university’s capacity for technology-enabled learning and supports PDP targets for innovation adoption and digital competitiveness.

3. Construction of a Fully Equipped DRRM Center and Campus Clinic

The Construction of the Fully Equipped DRRM Center and Campus Clinic creates a dedicated, two-storey disaster-resilient facility that serves as the campus’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and medical unit. It includes hazard-monitoring rooms, GIS mapping and early warning systems, an incident command center, training rooms, a secure storage warehouse for relief goods and emergency kits, rescue equipment storage, and a fully functional clinic for students, staff, and evacuees. The facility integrates solar panels and backup utilities to ensure continuous operation during disasters. This component responds to the operational failures observed during Typhoon Tino (November 2025), when the campus sheltered 362 evacuees but lacked proper emergency infrastructure, leading to operational challenges and ₱16.8 million in damages. The DRRM Center will institutionalize emergency preparedness, strengthen inter-agency coordination (with LGU Hinunangan, MDRRMO, PDRRMO, DSWD, DOH, BFP, PNP, and NGOs), and expand the campus’s role as a safe haven for disaster-prone communities.

Collectively, the SMART RESCUE Program supports multiple outcomes under the PDP 2023–2028 Results Matrix, including:

• Improved quality and resilience of education infrastructure (Chapter 2.2);
• Increased adoption of renewable energy and energy-efficient systems (Chapter 12);
• Strengthened innovation and digital transformation (Chapter 4);
• Reduced disaster risk and strengthened institutional and community resilience (Chapter 15).

The program is also aligned with the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan (RDP) and RDIP, which prioritize sustainable infrastructure, climate-resilient development, digital capacity upgrading, and preparedness in high-risk areas.

By integrating renewable energy expansion, ICT modernization, and disaster resilience infrastructure, SMART RESCUE ensures that SLSU–Hinunangan Campus can maintain academic continuity, protect its constituents, serve as a regional emergency partner, and function as a model for climate-responsive and technology-enabled higher education infrastructure.

column4: Establishment of Coastal Resource Facility w/ Aquatic Biology & Marine Biodiversity Research Laboratory
column6:
This project involves the establishment of a Coastal Resource Facility with an Aquatic Biology and Marine Biodiversity Research Laboratory at the SNSU–Malimono Campus. The facility is intended to serve as a specialized center for scientific instruction and research focusing on aquatic biology, marine ecosystems, coastal resource management, and biodiversity conservation. It will support activities such as biological assessment, species monitoring, applied biotechnology, molecular and cell biology, and bioinformatics. The project includes the construction of a two-storey building composed of four laboratories with stock rooms and officer-in-charge rooms, three classrooms, a Director’s Office, a conference room, male and female comfort rooms, PWD-accessible restrooms, an electrical room, and a ramp for universal accessibility. Environmental considerations such as energy and water conservation and proper waste management will be integrated into the building design, supported by existing road networks and drainage systems in the campus.

The establishment of this research and learning facility directly contributes to SNSU’s organizational outcomes by enhancing the delivery of relevant and quality tertiary education, strengthening higher education research, and increasing community engagement. The laboratories and classrooms will improve teaching and learning in marine and environmental sciences by providing modern, well-equipped spaces that support outcomes-based education and various forms of scientific investigation. The facility will also promote research productivity by enabling faculty and students to conduct studies addressing coastal degradation, marine biodiversity loss, climate change impacts, and public health concerns related to aquatic ecosystems—all of which align with the University’s mandate to generate innovations that advance economic productivity and environmental sustainability.

Furthermore, the facility will expand SNSU’s capacity to conduct extension programs, training sessions, and community-based initiatives that benefit coastal communities, particularly in disaster preparedness, sustainable fisheries, conservation practices, and resource management. By supporting instruction, research, and community outreach, the project addresses PDP 2023–2028 Subchapter 2.2 on improving education and lifelong learning, as well as key national goals on research, innovation, and environmental stewardship. Overall, the project will enable the University to respond to regional needs in coastal and marine resource management while advancing inclusive growth, environmental resilience, and human capital development.

column4: SLSU HTM - Learning Enhancement and Advancement Program (LEAP)
column6:
The SLSU HTM – Learning Enhancement and Advancement Program (LEAP) is a strategic academic and infrastructure development initiative designed to strengthen the quality, relevance, and future-readiness of Tourism Management education at Southern Leyte State University. The program consists of two major components: (1) the establishment of the SLSU iTRAVEL (Intelligent Tourism, Research, and Virtual Experience Laboratory), and (2) the creation of the Solar Power Farm and Renewable Energy Research Hub at the Main Campus. Together, these projects aim to enhance experiential learning, boost research and innovation capacity, and ensure sustainable campus operations aligned with national and regional development frameworks.

1. SLSU iTRAVEL (Intelligent Tourism, Research, and Virtual Experience Laboratory)

The first component, the SLSU iTRAVEL Laboratory, will serve as a dedicated academic, research, and innovation facility for the Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management program. The laboratory will house immersive virtual reality stations, digital tourism marketing studios, cultural intelligence modules, simulation areas for tourism operations, and analytics tools for sustainable destination management. By integrating these technologies, iTRAVEL will function as a transformative, future-oriented learning environment where students can apply global tourism practices, conduct tourism-related research, and engage in international collaborations. This facility addresses the current gap in specialized tourism laboratories that support technology-driven, sustainability-focused instruction. It also contributes directly to PDP-RM outcomes on improved higher education quality, enhanced innovation ecosystems, and strengthened tourism development in the regions.

2. Future-Proofing Campus Energy: Establishment of a Solar Power Farm and Renewable Energy Research Hub at Southern Leyte State University – Main Campus.

The second component, the Solar Power Farm and Renewable Energy Research Hub, involves constructing a renewable energy facility designed to generate 30–40% of the university’s electricity demand, reducing dependence on non-renewable energy sources and enhancing resilience against power interruptions. The solar farm will be complemented by a research and training hub equipped for renewable energy studies, policy research, prototype development, and capacity-building programs for students, faculty, LGUs, and partner agencies. This facility will also serve as a living laboratory for engineering, tourism, and allied programs to engage in interdisciplinary research on sustainability and climate action. This component supports PDP-RM outcomes related to sustainable infrastructure, green innovation, energy security, and climate resilience, aligned with Chapter 12 (Infrastructure), Chapter 15 (Climate Action and Resilience), and Chapter 8 (R&D, Technology, and Innovation) of the PDP 2023–2028.

Together, the two components of the SLSU LEAP Program address development gaps in instructional modernization, experiential learning, green campus operations, and applied research. The iTRAVEL Laboratory elevates the university’s capacity to deliver globally competitive Tourism Management education, while the Solar Farm and Research Hub strengthens institutional sustainability and promotes renewable energy leadership among SUCs in the region. The program is fully aligned with national development priorities under the PDP, RDP, and RDIP, contributing to outcomes on education quality, innovation, environmental sustainability, and regional economic growth. Through these integrated investments, the SLSU LEAP Program advances the University's vision of nurturing competent, compassionate, and future-ready graduates while modeling sustainability and technological innovation in higher education.

column4: Construction of Academic, Research, and Support Services Facilities of Southern Leyte State University - Maasin City Campus
column6:
The project involves the construction and operationalization of permanent academic, research, and support service facilities for Southern Leyte State University–Maasin City Campus (SLSU–MCC) to replace its current temporary and inadequate campus setup. Since its creation under Republic Act No. 11079 on September 27, 2018, the campus has relied on a commercial building formerly used as a motorcab terminal through a 10-year usufruct agreement with the City of Maasin, set to expire in FY 2028. For seven (7) years, SLSU–MCC has not received national infrastructure funding, resulting in a critical lack of classrooms, laboratories, research spaces, and student support facilities. Although the City of Maasin donated a 7-hectare site for campus development, it remains undeveloped due to financial constraints. The proposed project will serve as the University’s initial permanent infrastructure on this site and represents the foundation of the long-term Maasin City Campus development plan.

The project encompasses the construction of purpose-built academic buildings, research facilities, and support service structures, including upgraded electrical distribution systems and the installation of a solar photovoltaic power system to ensure energy efficiency and operational resilience. These facilities will house classrooms, laboratories, faculty spaces, student learning areas, administrative offices, and gender-responsive support amenities. Additionally, the project integrates climate-adaptive and sustainability features aligned with national green building priorities to ensure long-term durability and resilience.

The purpose of the project is to provide a functional, safe, and future-ready learning environment that supports high-quality instruction, research productivity, and student welfare—capabilities that the current temporary and leased structure cannot provide. By establishing permanent and modern academic infrastructure, the project enables SLSU–MCC to expand its program offerings, improve learning conditions, enhance faculty capabilities, and ensure continuity of academic operations beyond the expiry of the usufruct agreement in 2028.

This infrastructure investment directly contributes to PDP-RM outcomes under:

• PDP 2023–2028 Subchapter 2.2: Improve Education and Lifelong Learning, through expanded access to quality educational facilities and learning environments;

• Chapter 8: Advance Research, Development, and Innovation, through the creation of dedicated research spaces;

• Chapter 12: Expand and Upgrade Infrastructure, by building resilient, inclusive, and sustainable educational infrastructure; and

• Chapter 15: Accelerate Climate Action and Strengthen Disaster Resilience, through the integration of renewable energy systems and climate-resilient design.

The project is likewise aligned with the Eastern Visayas Regional Development Plan (RDP) and RDIP, supporting regional goals for human capital development, sustainable campus infrastructure, and equitable access to higher education. Through these investments, SLSU–MCC will transition from a temporary, resource-limited teaching facility to a permanent, fully functional academic institution capable of supporting instruction, research, and community development in Southern Leyte and beyond.

column4: Food and Technology Innovation Center
column6:
The project involves the construction of a new Food and Technology Innovation Center at the SNSU Main Campus in Brgy. Trinidad, Surigao City. The facility is envisioned as a modern learning and research hub that supports technological, social, and cultural innovation across the food value chain—from production, harvesting, and processing to manufacturing and distribution. Designed as a sustainable and climate-responsive structure, the center will incorporate energy- and water-conservation features, efficient waste management systems, and other environmental protection measures, supported by existing road networks and drainage systems in the new campus. The Center will provide state-of-the-art spaces for students, faculty, and partner industries to conduct research, develop innovative food products, explore biotechnology and molecular applications, and address emerging challenges in food safety, food security, and nutritional health.

The Food and Technology Innovation Center aims to strengthen SNSU’s role in food innovation, research, and development by providing specialized facilities, technical expertise, and support services that enhance the University’s capacity to generate new technologies and promote the commercialization of food-based innovations. The Center will assist local processing industries, microentrepreneurs, and community organizations in improving the quality, safety, and market competitiveness of food products. It will also support the development of high-impact research and training programs aimed at reducing malnutrition, promoting sustainable food systems, increasing productivity, and mitigating risks of outbreaks related to poor nutrition and food safety. By creating an environment that fosters innovation and applied research, the Center is expected to contribute to sustainable economic growth, local industry development, and community resilience.

The project supports multiple national priorities, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). It aligns with PDP 2023–2028 Subchapter 2.2 on improving education and lifelong learning, Subchapter 3.1 on ensuring food security and proper nutrition, Chapter 8 on advancing research and innovation, and Chapter 12 on expanding infrastructure. It also advances the 8-Point Socioeconomic Agenda by promoting job creation, enhancing food systems, supporting innovation-driven development, and mitigating socioeconomic vulnerabilities related to food supply and nutrition. Overall, the establishment of the Food and Technology Innovation Center will expand SNSU’s research capacity, strengthen academic-industry collaboration, support local economic development, and contribute to food security and sustainability in the Caraga Region.

column4: Completion of Two-Storey Agricultural Academic Building of NEMSU Tagbina Campus
column6:
With the full implementation of RA 10931 (UAQTEA) and UNIFAST, students coming from remote barangays and municipalities are expected to take the opportunity to enroll in the accredited and priority programs of NEMSU -Tagbina Campus.
At present, NEMSU Tagbina Campus has embraced an influx of students across all programs. With this trend being observed as a positive aspect of the institution, it incurs challenges as the current number of academic classrooms can no longer accommodate the students. Insufficient quantity of classrooms hindered the opportunity of the students to learn well because the learning environment is disturbed.
The College of Forestry, Agriculture and Aquatic Sciences (CFAAS) is currently dealing with this problem, and an immediate intervention is very necessary inorder to provide their students with better and conducive learning environment. The completion of this academic building will answer the need for additional classrooms the college is currently needed. In addition, this project will replace the aged academic building (but still utilized) that is deemed to be very fragile and can no longer withstand with any form of disaster or calamity.
In order to promote ease of access, the completion will still include important structures such as ramp-ups with railings for PWDs, GAD responsive facilities, gender responsive comfort rooms, fire detection and safety equipment, automatic emergency lights installed at strategic locations, dry type standpipe systems and sprinklers. For austerity measures, rainwater catchment facility will be materialized in support to water supply, which will use a 4,500L stainless steel tank to be placed above the rooftop.
Furniture and fixtures, needed appliances, landscaping and building permits and other related documents are among the packages in the rehabilitation project. In addition, solar electricity will be provided to support the continuous functionality of some essential equipment and facilities inside the building; it may also help avert the intermittent power supply in the locality.
The implementation of the project is proposed to commence in FY 2026. 
This proposed project is one of the steps of NEMSU Tagbina Campus in pushing its drive to modernization and standardization of academic community, as this move is embarked into university’s objectives, goals, visions and missions.

column4: Establishment of Marine and Underwater Research Center with Integrated Diving Facility
column6:
The Marine and Underwater Research Center will provide exciting opportunities and support for students, researchers, and startups to advance innovation and create greater value each individual and the community. The Marine and Underwater Research Center will house the Wet and Dry Laboratories including the Microbiology and Molecular Biology Laboratory (Figure 2). A training hall and additional rooms will be located at the upper floor. Aside from the laboratories, a provision for two units Diving facilities.

Features of the Marine and Underwater Research Center
1. Wet and Dry Laboratories
The wet laboratory will serve as an immediate access to seawater while the dry labs will be designed to instrument maintenance and data analysis. These spaces are designed for specific research needs. The wet lab will be used for handling and processing liquid samples, such as seawater, sediment, and biological specimens. It will be specialized facility equipped for conducting experiments and analyses on marine and aquatic organisms and samples. On the other hand, the dry lab will complement the wet lab and serve as a space for conducting data analysis, writing reports, and carrying out other research activities that do not involve handling liquid samples or live organisms

2. Microbiology and Molecular Laboratory
The Microbiology and Biomolecular Laboratory will provide the equipment and materials the researchers need to work with different biological samples for clinical, microbiological, and genetic studies. These laboratories can support researches on isolation of microorganisms such as fungi and bacteria; processing of blood, feces and urine samples; and extract DNA or RNA from marine samples – whatever is needed for research or health purposes.

3. Provision for Diving facility and motorpool
The diving facilities will allow researchers to directly observe and collect data on marine ecosystems, species, and habitats that are inaccessible from the surface. This will also provide opportunity for training and capacity building activities of researchers, students, and fisherfolks to receive traing in underwater research techniques. diving safety, and scientific diving protocols essential for developing a skilled workforce and promoting the responsible conduct of underwater research.

column4: Construction of Mini-Hotel - Del Carmen Campus
column6:
The Construction of a Mini-Hotel at the Surigao del Norte State University–Del Carmen Campus is proposed primarily as an instructional laboratory facility essential for the effective delivery of the Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management and Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management programs. These programs require a realistic, industry-based learning environment where students can acquire practical competencies alongside theoretical instruction, in accordance with outcomes-based education and industry standards.

The Mini-Hotel will function as a learning laboratory that simulates actual hospitality and tourism operations. It will provide structured spaces for hands-on training in hotel operations, front office services, housekeeping, food and beverage management, guest relations, and event management. By embedding experiential learning within the academic setting, the facility will significantly enhance instructional quality, curriculum implementation, and student preparedness for professional practice in the hospitality and tourism sectors.

In addition to its instructional function, the Mini-Hotel will serve as an academic support infrastructure for applied research, extension services, and community-based tourism initiatives in partnership with local government units, industry stakeholders, and tourism-related enterprises. It will also provide accommodation for visiting lecturers, researchers, extension personnel, and institutional partners, thereby supporting academic mobility, research collaboration, and extension outreach. As an income-generating facility, the Mini-Hotel will contribute to the sustainability of academic programs and university operations.

The project adopts climate-resilient and environmentally responsible design principles, incorporating energy-efficient systems and sustainable building practices. Overall, the Mini-Hotel strengthens higher education delivery by integrating instruction, research, extension, and income generation, while preparing graduates with industry-relevant skills that support inclusive local economic development and workforce readiness in the tourism and hospitality sector.

Furthermore, the project is envisioned as a skills-training and innovation hub for students, faculty, and community partners, including farmers, fisherfolk, cooperatives, and people’s organizations. By equipping students with competencies in automation, system integration, and intelligent machine design, the facility will help bridge the skills gap between academic training and industry requirements.

column4: Establishment of Drainage System Phase I of Phase II
column6:
Northern Bukidnon State College (NBSC) is located within the Tagoloan Mangima Watershed, part of the Tagoloan River basin covering 1,577 sq. km. The campus currently lacks a formal drainage system aside from a natural creek near the entrance. Manolo Fortich is crossed by three major rivers—Tagoloan, Mangima, and Agusan—that serve as natural drainage for the area.
The proposed drainage system at NBSC aims to manage stormwater runoff efficiently to protect infrastructure and ensure safety for students, faculty, and staff. It will feature a reinforced concrete open channel drainage line, approximately ___ meters long, routed mainly along campus roads near the SWDC building and low-lying areas. The system includes catch basins connected to reinforced concrete pipe culverts (RCPC) under the sidewalks.
The drainage channel will be 0.60 meters wide and 0.80 meters deep to handle peak flows and reduce overflow risks. Additional components include surface drains, covered concrete drains, sumps, and inspection chambers, all designed according to approved plans.
The Construction of Drainage System – Phase I will deliver outputs aligned with the approved plans, specifications, and implementation requirements. Under General Requirements, activities will include the mobilization and demobilization of resources, the establishment of necessary temporary facilities, and the full implementation of construction safety and health measures to ensure a secure work environment throughout the project duration. As-built drawings will also be prepared and submitted upon completion of works to reflect the actual conditions of the constructed system. For Site Works, tree removal within the designated alignment will be carried out, followed by the execution of approximately 887.15 cubic meters of structure excavation to properly prepare the foundation for the drainage structures. Under Plain and Reinforced Concrete Works, the project will involve the placement of 470.87 cubic meters of Class A structural concrete (28-day strength) and the installation of 39,678.63 kilograms of reinforcing steel bars, ensuring the required strength, stability, and long-term performance of the drainage system. Overall, Phase I will establish the initial structural components necessary to support the full development of the planned drainage network.

column4: Construction of Academic and Athletic Performance Development Complex for Student Wellness and Academic Excellence at Mindanao State University-Iligan Institute of Technology

column6:
The construction of the Academic and Athletic Performance Development Complex for Student Wellness and Academic Excellence at Mindanao State University–Iligan Institute of Technology will be the first of its kind in Iligan City. It will serve as a center for student wellness, holistic education, and excellence in both academics and athletics, fostering a balanced environment where learners can thrive intellectually, physically, and emotionally. Spanning a total floor area of 29,822.94 square meters, the complex will feature five key facilities: 

A. MSU-IIT Academic Track and Field Complex (P 70,000,000) - Designed with an Olympic-sized oval track, the facility serves as the primary training ground for sprints, relays, and long-distance running, while also accommodating field events such as jumping and throwing disciplines. Beyond track and field, the expansive oval integrates open spaces suitable for soccer and other football sports. A modern space for athletic training and competitions. This project envisions creating an olympic-sized track and field complex that meets international standars. It seeks not merely to serve MSU-IIT but also to become a hub for athletic development in the region, fostering community engagement, enhancing the training environment, and providing a venue capable of hosting significant sports events.

B. MSU-IIT Wellness and Physical Education Learning Hub (P 45,000,000) - This serves as a multi-purpose facility dedicated to advancing student health, fitness, and holistic development. The facility is designed to accommodate 100–150 students, providing an ideal venue for physical education classes and a variety of sports activities such as Karate, Arnis, Dance Studio, and Indoor Badminton. The Wellness Center extends beyond MSU-IIT's boundaries to serve the wider commnuity of Iligan City and Northern Mindanao. It is designed as a comprehensive hub for physical, mental, and social well-being, supporting a holistoc approach to wellness that complements academic pursuits and fosters broader community engagement.

C. Student Athletes' Quarter and Academic Lecture Hall (P 125,000,000) - This facility is envisioned as a dynamic and nurturing environment where young athletes can not only be housed in their dedicated quarters and trained but also grow holistically while pursuing their academic aspirations. With a seating capacity of 3,000, the big lecture hall provides ample space to accommodate students for academic lectures, conferences, and symposiums. It addresses not only the needs of MSU-IIT's athletes but also those from local schools and colleges across Northern Mindanao. The facility would significantly enhance the university's ability to hist large-scale events, promoting community engemenet, and economic growth through sports and cultural activities.

D. Physical Education Learning and Activity Area (P 6,000,000) - Designed for recreational and competitive tennis matches. It is also an extra space for other extra curricular activities such as group dancing, and other academic requirements.

E. Integrated Aquatic Fitness and Learning Facility (P 85,000,000) - This facility supports physical education and academic instruction through swimming, water safety, and aquatic sports. With a 700-seat bleacher, it serves as a vital venue for structured swimming classes, combining academic learning with athletic training. 

Strategically located at the Hinaplanon Annex Campus, construction will commence in FY 2027, divided into two phases to ensure implementation and sustainability.

column4: Business Education Complex Development: Strategic Infrastructure   Investment for Sustainable Higher Education
column5: Carlos C. Hilado Memorial State University
column6:
The “Business Education Complex Development: Strategic Infrastructure Investment for Sustainable Higher Education” is a long-term, multi-phased infrastructure initiative that will strengthen the academic environment and modernize learning systems for business education and related fields. It is anchored on the institution’s Land Use Development and Investment Program (LUDIP) and aligned with national higher education modernization policies, integrating gender-responsive, inclusive, and green design principles throughout its implementation.

From Fiscal Year 2026 to 2028, the business education complex development program will deliver a cohesive infrastructure ecosystem comprising new three-storey academic buildings, an integrated four-storey building for academic support facilities, and a modernized multi-purpose auditorium, all fully compliant with statutory and regulatory requirements and equipped with internationalization-ready features to support the academe's global engagements and international affairs.

This strategic initiative encompasses three interrelated projects implemented sequentially through a programmatic, phased approach with meticulously defined scopes of work:

Project No. 1: Construction of a 3-Storey Academic Building with 12 Smart Classrooms 

Scope of Work

A.	Planning & Pre-Construction
1.	Preparation of Detailed Engineering Design (DED) and comprehensive architectural plans integrating structural, electrical, plumbing, ICT, and green building features.
2.	Securing environmental compliance (ECC), building permits, and safety clearances.
3.	Conducting stakeholder consultations for gender-inclusive, PWD-accessible, and student-centered design validation.
B.	Construction
1.	Structural development of the Phase 1A portion of the 3-story academic building
2.	Construction of 12 Smart Classrooms equipped with interactive learning displays, energy-efficient HVAC/lighting, acoustic treatments, solar-ready conduits, LED systems, low-flow fixtures, natural daylighting, and optimized ventilation
3.	Installation of gender-inclusive/PWD-accessible comfort rooms and universal access features (ramps, tactile paving, handrails, accessible entrances).
C.	Post-Construction
1.	Furnishing classrooms with ergonomic, modular furniture and digital tools (interactive boards, projectors, Wi-Fi infrastructure).
2.	Comprehensive utilities testing, building commissioning, and turnover orientation for faculty/staff and building custodial teams
3.	Final safety inspections and securing Occupancy Certificate

Project No. 2: Completion of Annex 3-storey Academic Building with 15 Smart 
                         Classrooms 

Scope of Work

A.	Planning & Pre-Construction
1.	Harmonizing architectural and engineering designs with Phase 1A for visual and structural continuity.
2.	Securing permits and planning structural integration for seamless campus connectivity.
3.	Conducting consultations with faculty and administrators to optimize office layouts and functionality.
B.	Construction
1.	Developing a three-storey Annex Building directly linked to the Phase 1A core structure.
2.	Constructing 15 ICT-integrated, energy-efficient smart classrooms.
3.	Establishing modern faculty offices per floor
4.	Expanding circulation systems, including covered walkways, hallways, and movement networks.
5.	Incorporating PWD-accessible features and gender-inclusive comfort rooms.
6.	Implementing climate-resilient design elements such as optimized ventilation, shading devices, and heat-reflective materials.
C.	Post-Construction
1.	Furnishing classrooms with ergonomic, modular furniture and digital tools (interactive boards, projectors, Wi-Fi infrastructure).
2.	Installing ICT connectivity systems and digital teaching tools
3.	Training for faculty and staff on facility management and technology utilization
4.	Conducting comprehensive building commissioning, systems testing, final turnover, occupancy certification

Project 3: Construction of Academic Support Facilities  

Scope of Work 

A.	Planning & Pre-Construction
1.	Preparing a unified architectural, structural, and engineering design covering:
•	Library/Learning Hub
•	Business, Accounting and Finance laboratories
•	Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Data Analytics Centers
•	MSME Center and Internationalization Hub
•	Student collaboration areas, canteen, and outdoor learning spaces
•	Multi-Purpose Activity Auditorium
•	GAD and child-minding center
•	Physical Management unit
•	NSTP and ROTC office
•	International and Global Engagement Center
•	Conference and Meeting Rooms
2.	Ensuring alignment with CHED Laboratory Standards, ISO 21001 (Learning Organization Management), and ICT industry standards.
3.	Preparing and complying with the Environmental & Social Management Plan (ESMP).
4.	Conducting Gender and Development (GAD) and accessibility reviews to guarantee inclusive design.
5.	Planning campus circulation, including ramps, wide hallways, elevators, and other universal accessibility features.
6.	Integration of green building measures such as passive ventilation, daylighting, rainwater harvesting, low-VOC materials, and energy-efficient systems.
B.	Construction
1.	Construct the Integrated he Integrated Academic Support Facility to house the Library/Learning Hub, Business and Accounting Laboratories, Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Data Analytics Centers, MSME Research Center, Internationalization Hub, student collaboration areas, canteen, and outdoor learning spaces. Execute all works per approved structural and architectural plans, including modern furniture, fixtures, and equipment; expanded circulation systems (covered walkways, hallways, movement networks); PWD-friendly features; gender-inclusive comfort rooms; and climate-resilient elements like optimized ventilation, shading devices, and heat-reflective materials.
2.	Transform the existing gymnasium into an Enhanced Multi-Purpose Activity Auditorium with modern, flexible modular seating for lectures, workshops, banquets, and conferences; acoustically engineered walls and ceilings; an elevated stage featuring podium, LED backdrop, and customizable lighting; high-definition AV systems with multi-screen projection, livestreaming, and centralized control room; interpretation/translation booths; VIP/reception areas; and conference-grade audio for global events. Integrate accessibility features (wheelchair ramps, stage lifts, priority seating, Braille signage, tactile guides, gender-inclusive restrooms); sustainable practices (passive lighting/ventilation, solar-ready systems, rainwater harvesting, greywater reuse, low-VOC materials, climate-resilient build); safety/security systems (fire detection/suppression, alarms, earthquake-resistant design, CCTV, integrated security); and ancillary spaces (backstage, storage, control booths, VIP lounges, exhibition lobby for student/faculty showcases).
C.	Post-Construction
1.	Complete interior fit-out and furnishing, including the provision and placement of modern furniture, fixtures, and equipment (FF&E) in all new spaces.
2.	Finalize installation, configuration, and testing of all specialized ICT systems and digital learning tools to ensure full functionality and integration.

7.	Provide orientation and capacity-building for faculty, staff, and building personnel on facility operations, safety protocols, and effective use of installed technologies.

column4: CHMSU-ALIJIS ASCEND : ( Academic, Science, and Campus Expansion for Next-Generation Development) Program
column5: Carlos C. Hilado Memorial State University
column6:
The CHMSU-ALIJIS ASCEND Program is proposed in response to the increasing academic, laboratory, and technical capacity requirements of the Alijis Campus. Over the past years, the campus has experienced significant growth in student enrollment, particularly in Science, Technology, Engineering, and General Education programs. This surge in population has strained existing facilities, resulting in overcrowded classrooms, inadequate laboratory spaces, and insufficient specialized environments required to support practical, research-based, and skills-oriented learning.

At present, the campus infrastructure is no longer aligned with the modern standards of instructional delivery and safety, nor is it sufficient to support the expansion of academic programs mandated under institutional development goals. Many classrooms are operating beyond optimal capacity, and existing laboratories lack the functionality, safety provisions, and equipment-ready configurations needed to meet CHED and industry requirements for Science and Engineering education. Without strategic infrastructure intervention, the campus will be unable to match projected enrollment increases, comply with accreditation standards, or sustain the quality of learning outcomes expected from a rapidly evolving educational environment.

The ASCEND Program directly addresses these gaps by consolidating the construction of three critical infrastructure projects: the Three-Storey Laboratory Annex Building, the Four-Storey Academic Building, and the Three-Storey Engineering Building. These facilities are designed to provide modern, multi-storey, and multi-functional academic spaces that meet the demands of current and future students. The program aims to expand instructional capacity, enhance laboratory-based teaching and research, and strengthen engineering education through dedicated, safe, and industry-aligned learning environments.

Furthermore, the program adopts a phased construction strategy to ensure efficient resource allocation, minimize disruption to existing campus operations, and align with budgetary and implementation timelines required under the PIPOLS framework. The consolidated approach allows the institution to prioritize infrastructure investments that yield the highest academic and operational benefit, while ensuring that each project complements the overall campus development roadmap.

The CHMSU-ALIJIS ASCEND Program is not only a response to immediate infrastructure deficiencies but also a strategic investment in long-term institutional resilience and competitiveness. By modernizing and expanding the campus facilities, the program supports broader national goals on advancing science and technology education, fostering innovation, and strengthening human capital development. It positions the Alijis Campus to deliver higher-quality academic services, accommodate future growth, and provide equitable access to safe, well-equipped, and future-ready learning spaces.

In essence, the program is critical to ensuring that the institution remains responsive to emerging educational demands, compliant with regulatory standards, and capable of producing graduates equipped with the competencies required in a knowledge-driven economy. The CHMSU-ALIJIS ASCEND Program serves as a foundational step toward building a more resilient, innovative, and forward-looking academic environment for the next generation of learners.

The construction of the 4-storey classroom building is aligned with the Caraga State University LIKHA Agenda, particularly in advancing Leadership and Good Governance, Innovation and Relevance, Knowledge Co-creation, and Human Capital Development. It is consistent with the University’s mandate under Republic Act No. 9854, supports the objectives of the Higher Education Act of 1994 (RA 7722), and aligns with national priorities under the Philippine Development Plan 2023–2028 on expanding and upgrading educational infrastructure.

In line with these national development goals, the University of the Philippines (UP), as the National University, is obliged to relate its research, graduate, and public service activities to these “needs of the Filipino people and their aspirations for social progress and transformation” (Section 8 of RA 9500, University of the Philippines Charter of 2008). With capabilities in various fields of expertise, UP is well suited to provide opportunities for advanced studies, basic and applied research and development, as well as scholarly and technical assistance to the government, the private sector, and civil society to further the interventions necessary to achieve the inclusive growth envisioned in the Philippine Development Plan.

As the host locality and the third largest regional contributor to national output, Region 3 Central Luzon envisions an Enhanced “W” Growth Corridor, requiring the expansion of potentials in tourism, the industrial heartland, and high value crops and agro-forestry, complemented by the conversion of lahar-laden areas. Priority projects have thus been identified for improving physical access to tourism destinations, improving postharvest and value-adding processes of the agricultural corridor, strengthening sound environmental management and disaster risk reduction to support both the mining and agriculture sectors, as well as providing world-oriented higher education and training in English proficiency, technical skills, and entrepreneurial knowledge to propel the ICT and logistics industries (Central Luzon Regional Development Plan 2011-2016, NEDA Region 3).

With tertiary enrollment rates rising by about 6% per year and more than half of all tertiary students enrolling in public institutions (PSA Education Statistics), higher education needs to meet industry- specific demands of a changing business landscape to further the national goal of inclusive growth. An academic hub for inter-, multi-, and trans-disciplinary studies can provide updated information and training along with highly specialized knowledge and skills in programs integrating different fields. The opportunities for applied research that are relevant and practical or appropriate for specific industry needs will provide a magnet for development that will address the primordial concern of serving the nation by advancing these regional requirements.
