column4: Establishment of Athletics and Sports Complex (Phase I)
column6:
The Athletics and Sports Complex of Surigao del Norte State University (SNSU) is envisioned as a core academic support program that strengthens quality education and lifelong learning, with particular emphasis on the instructional, laboratory, and training requirements of the Bachelor of Physical Education (BPEd) program. The program directly supports the improvement of learning environments, learner well-being, and holistic student development, consistent with national education priorities.

Anchored on PDP Subchapter 2.2, which emphasizes learner well-being, inclusive access to quality education, and the development of life skills, the program provides an enabling environment where physical education, sports development, leadership formation, and health promotion are fully integrated into the academic experience. The complex will serve as a learning platform for General Education courses (Physical Education and NSTP), Bachelor of Physical Education instruction, teacher education, sports science–related learning activities, and student leadership training, while also supporting faculty development and lifelong learning initiatives.

The facility is designed to function not merely as a venue for athletic competitions, but as a learning-centered space that promotes discipline, teamwork, resilience, gender equality, and inclusive participation among students, faculty, and staff. By embedding classrooms beneath the bleachers, the program directly links theory and practice, allowing structured academic instruction, coaching clinics, officiating courses, sports management training, and skills assessment to be conducted within a single, integrated learning environment. This configuration is particularly essential in ensuring the attainment of the competency-based outcomes of the Bachelor of Physical Education program.

The Athletics and Sports Complex also supports inclusive and equitable education by ensuring equal access for men, women, and persons with disabilities (PWDs), consistent with national education reforms and the PDP’s emphasis on reducing disparities in learning opportunities. Beyond formal degree instruction, the program fosters lifelong learning by opening the facility to community-based sports training, wellness programs, in-service training for teachers and coaches, and continuing education activities that encourage sustained participation in physical activity across all age groups.

Through this program, SNSU enhances the delivery of the Bachelor of Physical Education and related academic offerings, strengthens student engagement and retention, and contributes to the formation of physically healthy, socially responsible, and professionally competent graduates—fully aligned with the objectives of PDP 2023–2028 Subchapter 2.2.

column4: Completion of Multi-purpose Building (Dormitory)
column6:
The Completion of the Multi-purpose Building (Dormitory) of Surigao del Norte State University (SNSU) is a learner-centered support program designed to strengthen quality education, equitable access to learning, and student well-being, consistent with the objectives of Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, Subchapter 2.2 – Improve Education and Lifelong Learning.

Anchored on PDP Subchapter 2.2, which emphasizes inclusive access to education, learner welfare, and improved learning environments, the project provides on-campus residential facilities that directly support students’ academic participation, retention, and completion. The dormitory serves as an essential component of the university’s learning ecosystem by ensuring that students—particularly those coming from geographically distant, economically disadvantaged, or vulnerable backgrounds—have safe, affordable, and accessible housing within the campus.

The program recognizes that adequate student housing is integral to educational quality. By reducing travel time, transportation costs, and exposure to safety risks, the dormitory enables students to focus on their academic responsibilities, participate more actively in academic and co-curricular activities, and benefit from extended access to learning resources, faculty consultations, and student support services. This environment supports sustained engagement in learning and promotes academic success.

Beyond accommodation, the Multi-purpose Building (Dormitory) is designed to function as a learning-support space that promotes discipline, responsibility, character formation, and communal living—values essential to lifelong learning. Shared facilities and regulated residence systems foster social interaction, peer learning, and personal development under conditions conducive to academic pursuits.

Consistent with national education reforms and Republic Act No. 11396 (LUDIP Act), which mandates State Universities and Colleges to provide campus residences, the project institutionalizes student housing as a permanent academic support mechanism. The dormitory is designed to be gender-responsive and inclusive, with provisions for male and female students and accessibility features for persons with disabilities (PWDs), reinforcing the PDP’s goal of reducing inequalities in access to education.

The facility also adopts environmentally adaptive and resilient design features, including water and energy conservation measures and proper waste management systems, ensuring a safe, healthy, and sustainable learning environment that supports students’ physical and mental well-being.

Through the completion of the Multi-purpose Building (Dormitory), SNSU strengthens its capacity to deliver quality, inclusive, and learner-centered education, improves student retention and completion rates, and supports lifelong learning by providing an enabling residential environment aligned with the goals of PDP 2023–2028 Subchapter 2.2.

column4: Water Filtration and Treatment facility
column5: Dr. Emilio B. Espinosa, Sr. Memorial State College of Agriculture and Technology
column6: The project involves the construction of a dedicated sanitary structure and the installation of a multi-stage water filtration and treatment system. It includes civil works for the housing facility, installation of storage tanks, pumps, and a distribution network. The facility is designed to treat raw water from the Mabigo watershed, removing turbidity, odor, and harmful solids to produce clean, non-potable water. This treated water will be utilized for daily activities such as laboratory experiments, comfort room flushing, general cleaning, and sanitation requirements of the infirmary, ensuring a hygienic campus environment. The construction of a Water Filtration and Treatment Facility is urgent to address the deteriorating quality of the college's general water supply. Currently, the campus buildings are supplied by the Mabigo watershed through an existing piping system; however, this supply is frequently characterized by high turbidity and significant levels of dissolved and undissolved solids. This poor water quality disrupts daily operations in several critical ways. Specifically, the water is unsuitable for washing laboratory glassware or conducting basic experiments due to contaminants. Furthermore, water used in comfort rooms often exhibits bad odor and discoloration, rendering facilities unsanitary and unpleasant. Crucially, the newly constructed infirmary requires a reliable supply of clean, clear water for general hygiene and medical sanitation, which the current source cannot provide. Consequently, this project aims to treat the water to a level safe for these daily activities, preventing the staining of fixtures, clogging of pipes, and potential skin irritations, while supporting the operational needs of the college.

column4: CONSTRUCTION OF A TWO‑STOREY MACHINE SHOP BUILDING
column5: Zamboanga State College of Marine Sciences and Technology
column6:
Zamboanga State College of Marine Sciences and Technology (ZSCMST), as a premier institution for marine sciences and technology in Western Mindanao, is mandated to provide quality education and training that meet both national and international maritime standards. Central to this mission is the College of Maritime Education (CME), which delivers programs in marine engineering and related disciplines that require hands-on laboratory training in machining, fabrication, and engine maintenance.

The institution currently operates the Machine Engineering Workshop A, identified in the ZSCMST LUDIP (Draft v5, pp. 217, 226) as part of its existing academic support facilities. While this workshop has served as the backbone of practical training for maritime students, it is limited in both capacity and functionality. Its single-floor structure cannot adequately support the demands of increasing student enrollment, nor can it accommodate the installation of modern technical equipment required under CHED–MARINA Memorandum Circulars and the Standards of Training, Certification, and Watchkeeping for Seafarers (STCW).

The lack of sufficient laboratory space also creates safety concerns, as multiple student groups must often share limited equipment and facilities. Moreover, the absence of integrated briefing and debriefing areas undermines the effectiveness of laboratory instruction, which requires not only technical practice but also structured academic reinforcement.

To address these challenges, ZSCMST proposes the construction of a Two-Storey Machine Shop. This facility is designed to maximize available land while providing dedicated spaces for both laboratory and academic functions. The Ground Floor will serve as the primary laboratory area, equipped for machining, welding, and fabrication training. The Second Floor will provide lecture rooms and briefing/debriefing areas, ensuring that theoretical instruction is seamlessly integrated with hands-on practice.

By upgrading its existing workshop into a modern two-storey facility, ZSCMST will:
a)	Expand its capacity to accommodate projected enrollment growth,
b)	Enhance compliance with CHED–MARINA and STCW facility standards,
c)	Improve safety and instructional quality, and
d)	Strengthen its institutional competitiveness as a provider of maritime engineering education.

The proposed Two-Storey Machine Shop is therefore not only a response to present gaps but also a strategic investment in ZSCMST’s long-term academic and training capacity.

Needs Analysis
The College of Maritime Education (CME) has experienced remarkable enrollment growth, rising from 888 students in SY 2020–2021 to 1,835 in SY 2025–2026, an increase of 106.64% in just five years. This equates to an average annual growth rate of 15.67%, with projections indicating that CME enrollment could surpass 3,280 students by 2030 if current trends continue. Table 1 shows enrollment data spanning five School Years.

The facility will also support research, extension, and innovation initiatives related to educational technology, teacher training, and skills development.

Aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 4 and 9, the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, Regional Development Plan (RDP), the Higher Education Transformation (THE) Agenda, and the university’s LIKHA Agenda, the project contributes to strengthening human capital, advancing digital transformation, and improving equitable access to quality education. column4: Completion of University Gymnasium and Cultural Center - Phase II
column6:
The Gymnasium Improvement Project is designed as a climate-resilient, modern, and industrialized facility that significantly enhances functionality, accessibility, comfort, and user experience. The project involves a comprehensive set of upgrades and renovations aimed at transforming the existing gymnasium into a state-of-the-art sports and cultural facility capable of serving the growing needs of the University and the wider community.

Key components of the project include the extension of the bleachers by 3.7 meters on both sides, increasing the seating capacity by approximately 700 additional persons and bringing the total capacity to 1,500 individuals. To improve indoor comfort and ventilation, existing casement windows will be replaced with awning windows, complemented by the installation of six whirlwind roof ventilators to enhance natural air circulation. The air conditioning system will be upgraded with the addition of air coolers to ensure effective temperature control during major events, while Acoustic PE Foam roof insulation will be installed to reduce noise levels and improve energy efficiency. The indoor basketball court will be expanded to accommodate larger games and events in accordance with modern sports standards.

Architecturally, the gymnasium will feature a redesigned and beautified façade inspired by the iconic balangay boat, symbolizing the rich local culture and heritage of the Caraga Region. The roofing form evokes the shape of the boat and its sail, reinforcing the structure’s cultural identity while maintaining structural grandeur. The building is designed as a green and well-oriented facility, maximizing natural lighting and ventilation to reduce energy consumption during daytime use. The surrounding landscape will be carefully planned to complement the expansive green environment of Caraga State University, further enhancing the overall visual and environmental quality of the campus.

column4: Public-Private Partnerships for School Infrastructure Project (PSIP Connect Lite)
column6:
Despite sustained investments in basic education, digital access in public schools remains limited. Only a minority of schools have reliable broadband, and most learners lack regular access to personal learning devices. These gaps contributed to learning losses, weak digital literacy, and poor international learning outcomes.

Conventional procurement approaches cannot deliver integrated devices, connectivity, platforms, training, and lifecycle maintenance at scale within annual budget constraints. PSIP Connect Lite adopts a Public-Private Partnership model to bundle these components under a single performance-based contract.

As an unsolicited proposal, the project introduces an integrated, equity-financed solution designed to pilot a scalable national model under PSIP Connect, while transferring technology, financing, and operational risks to the private sector.

column4: PSIP Connect Pilot - Project LEARN (Last-mile Education Access and Resilience Network)
column6:
PROJECT LEARN responds to persistent education infrastructure gaps not fully addressed by traditional classroom-focused programs. While the classroom backlog remains significant, access to reliable connectivity, devices, and power has emerged as a critical constraint to learning outcomes, especially in last-mile schools.

Drawing from lessons learned under earlier PSIP phases, the Department of Education adopted a PPP model with managed services to address digital access, lifecycle maintenance, and operational reliability. PROJECT LEARN expands the scope of PSIP beyond physical classrooms by prioritizing connectivity-first interventions, complemented by optional Smart Classrooms and renewable energy systems.

The project supports DepEd’s shift toward blended learning, digital resilience, and inclusive education delivery, while ensuring fiscal discipline and risk transfer through a performance-based PPP structure.

column4: PSIP Connect Pilot - Allied Digital Education Ecosystem Program (ADEEP)
column6:
The Department received an Unsolicited Proposal on 28 November 2025 from Allied Corporation Asia Pacific, with Google and PLDT as subcontracting partners, entitled the Allied Digital Education Ecosystem Program (ADEEP). The proposal seeks to accelerate the digitalization of basic education delivery in 1,000 selected public schools in Region IV-A.

The project targets approximately 24,000 teachers and 285,500 Grade 4 learners. It includes the provision of around 24,000 Chromebook devices for teachers and 9,500 Chromebook devices for learners, supported by 400 e-carts, ensuring a 1:1 device-to-teacher ratio in pilot schools. The proposal also covers a cloud-native learning and asset management platform to support e-learning delivery, secure digital assessments, real-time asset tracking, and data-driven decision-making.

These are complemented by guaranteed 300 Mbps broadband connectivity with redundancy, reliable power solutions, mandatory teacher capacity-building through Google Accreditation programs, and the establishment of a local repair and maintenance facility to ensure sustainability and timely after-sales support.

column4: Last Mile Schools Green Energy and Connectivity Project (Project ARAL)
column6:
With the lack or absence of reliable power supply, these schools often have no internet connection which limits the students’ access to educational materials and information from the internet which could help them in their educational needs and development. 
The Inter-Agency Energy Efficiency and Conservation Committee (IAEECC) passed Resolution No. 8, Series of 2023 which urged government agencies, including government-owned and controlled corporations, state universities and colleges, and local government units to install solar panels on their buildings.

The DepEd is in need of electric energy and internet connectivity for these schools and desires that this be sourced from solar energy.
Project ARAL aims to supply laptops and Smart TV, provide Hybrid Solar System and satellite internet that will supply electric energy and internet connection to 9,788 classrooms in Last Mile Schools (LMS) in Region VII and VIII (excluding Negros Oriental and Siquijor) through an Unsolicited Build-Lease-Transfer (BLT) modality under the PPP Code.
